articles.title: Belgium's Novadip Biosciences raises €10.4 million to fund pivotal clinical trial and unlock EIB loan tranche | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Novadip Biosciences, a Belgian late-stage clinical BioTech company specialising in regenerative medicine, has closed a €10.4 million (roughly $12 million) convertible financing round.
The round was led by US-based New Science Ventures, with participation from a syndicate of Novadip’s existing backers, including Fund+, Wallonie Entreprendre, VIVES Fund, ORSA Tech, Sambrinvest, Noshaq and Invest.BW. The financing follows the company securing a €9.6 million convertible loan last year, bringing the total to €20 million in convertible financing since June 2025.
“This financing is a strong vote of confidence from our investors, and I’d like to thank them for their ongoing support. This is an important step forward for Novadip. It provides the resources to advance NVD003 through several major clinical and regulatory milestones, including the completion of our pivotal Phase 3 program in congenital pseudarthrosis of the tibia and the preparation for regulatory submission in the United States,” said Dr. Denis Dufrane, founder and CEO of Novadip.
Founded in Belgium in 2013 as a spin-off from Université Catholique de Louvain and St. Luc University Hospital, Novadip grew out of research by its founder, Dr. Dufrane. The company has built a proprietary platform, known as 3M³, that uses adipose-derived stem cells arranged within a three-dimensional extracellular matrix to create tissue capable of healing large bone defects, non-union fractures and spinal fusion cases in a single procedure.
Its test pipeline is built on two candidates: NVDOO3 and NVDX3. The NVD003, which is at the heart of this financing round, is a moldable, autologous graft built from a patient’s own stem cells, designed to be implanted within three months of cell collection. The company says it has already shown durable bone fusion at 24 months and mobility maintained up to four-year follow-up.
The company’s second candidate, NVDX3, an allogenic (donor-derived) bone grafting material, has completed Phase 1b/2a trials in trauma surgery and spinal fusion, and has FDA clearance to begin a Phase 2b/3 trial.
The financing will primarily support the completion of a pivotal Phase 3 trial of NVD003 for congenital pseudarthrosis of the tibia (CPT), a rare and difficult-to-treat pediatric bone condition. The trial is already running in both the United States and the European Union.
The funds will also cover preparation of a Biologics License Application (BLA) to the US Food and Drug Administration, and support the company’s push toward what it calls “value-creating milestones”, including potential strategic partnerships and, if the BLA is approved, a Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher from the FDA, which the company values at more than $100 million.
“With a pivotal Phase 3 program underway, regulatory preparation advancing and a significant commercial opportunity, Novadip is entering a critical value-creating period. This financing provides the means to execute on these priorities and prepare the business for its next stage of development,” said Eric Pâques, Chairman of the Board.
Novadip is aiming to obtain market authorisation for NVD003 in congenital pseudarthrosis of the tibia by 2028, followed by approval for adults with critical-size bone defects by 2031.
Novadip says hitting the €10.4 million target opens access to a tranche of an €18 million venture debt agreement Novadip signed in 2023 with the European Investment Bank, backed by the European Union’s InvestEU programme. It now employs 53 people and has raised €137 million in equity and non-dilutive funding since inception.

articles.title: 4 ways to address the failures we found along the US border’s “virtual wall”
articles.text:
4 ways to address the failures we found along the US border’s “virtual wall”
The US has spent billions on surveillance towers, but hundreds of people have died near them. Here’s how to strengthen federal oversight.
MIT Technology Review today published our investigation into how many people have died near the “virtual wall” of surveillance towers that the US government has installed along the US-Mexico border.
We found cases of people who walked undetected through areas surveilled by advanced, AI-enabled towers and later died nearby, where their bodies remained unnoticed for weeks or months. These cases reflect systemic flaws in the virtual wall: broken towers, algorithms that failed to detect people, and agents who simply did not respond to alerts.
This story is part of Dying on Camera, a collaboration between MIT Technology Review and Times of San Diego. Journalists in both newsrooms spent the past year examining the failures of border surveillance technology and uncovering the stories of the people who die in the borderlands.
Each of these deaths should have raised alarms inside US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) about the flaws in the agency’s surveillance network. This is particularly true for cases near the latest towers built by the defense company Anduril, which continues to win major contracts and is poised to benefit from the windfall of federal money slated for border security. The US is set to spend $1 billion to triple the size of the virtual wall by 2034.
Here are four ideas for what CBP should do next to address these failures.
1. Conduct a comprehensive audit of deaths near the virtual wall
“If I were the federal government, I would do an audit, because this feels like it’s not working.”
That was New Mexico state representative Sarah Silva’s reaction when MIT Technology Review showed her that in 2024 alone, more than 18 people had died near surveillance towers in just one small stretch of desert near her district.
An audit is necessary because, despite poring over thousands of pages of police reports and other documents about surveillance towers, we have only limited knowledge of how many towers are out there and where they’re located.
CBP does not publish a comprehensive map of its virtual wall. We instead relied on mapping work led by the nonprofit Electronic Frontier Foundation and then used satellite imagery to verify where specific towers were and approximately when they were installed.
We analyzed lots of towers—nearly 600. But that’s still far less than the 800 the government says operate today. And our estimates of when they went up are inexact. That means our tally of more than 1,050 people who have died near them is an undercount. And we don’t have a complete picture of where along the border the problem is worst.
An internal audit would not have such limitations. In theory, CBP tracks when each tower went up and when it was active. It has had the ability to audit their effectiveness—while quantifying how many people have died near them—since at least 2015, when it began installing the types of towers included in our analysis. But sources told us it has never done such an audit. Our findings make the need for one more urgent.
2. Fix the way the agency tracks migrant deaths and remains
If CBP is to analyze instances where people have died near its surveillance technology, it needs to know when and where those deaths happen. And the current system for tracking that data is beyond broken.
As we note in our methodology, there is no national agency that collects and publishes all available records on migrant deaths. We sifted through thousands of pages of records from dozens of agencies in Texas alone, and our picture is still incomplete owing to the lack of a shared protocol for documenting these deaths in public records.
Border Patrol has had its own internal system, called the Border Safety Initiative Tracking System (BSITS), in place since 2007. But it wasn't until 2021 that national rules were established for how different sectors should enter cases into the system. The next year, the Government Accountability Office (GAO) found that many cases still weren't being tracked in this system, especially deaths that weren't discovered by Border Patrol. In 2023, the GAO reported that Border Patrol has taken steps to fix that, but outside researchers consistently find the agency’s estimates to be undercounts even today.
In addition to tracking migrant deaths, CBP launched a program in 2017 to prevent them, called the Missing Migrant Program. In April 2025, the GAO found the program was improving the way it collected and tracked data about events like 911 calls and rescues. The problem, it said, was that there was no plan in place to use the data to measure whether the program was actually increasing rescues or reducing deaths, which are its primary goals. It made two recommendations for solutions, neither of which has been implemented.
3. Track cases when surveillance technology leads to an apprehension
In 2014, when the virtual wall was much smaller, the GAO suggested that Border Patrol agents log when a piece of technology helped them apprehend someone who was trying to enter the US illegally. It would take agents some extra time, but logging these assists would help Congress understand how often various surveillance technologies were leading to actual apprehensions. Once this data was collected, GAO added, the agency should measure whether its surveillance technologies were working. CBP agreed, and it started requiring agents to enter such information.
Then, in 2017, the GAO reported that the data being collected was inaccurate and unreliable; it found agents in Texas, for example, who were crediting a specific type of tower in apprehensions hundreds of times, even though no such towers existed anywhere in the state. Border Patrol again said it would improve; it agreed to train agents on the importance of collecting such information.
But years later, agents told us, it’s still not a priority. One former CBP official described the mandate as “spitting in the wind, to be honest,” and said the messy reality of apprehensions doesn't translate into neat metrics. (The official, who requested anonymity, served during the Biden administration and wasn’t authorized to discuss sensitive issues.)
And in August 2021, more than seven years after it agreed to do so, CBP still had not produced any analysis on the towers’ effectiveness (it finished one in 2022, the GAO notes, but the results are not public).
That means the virtual wall is growing faster than anyone is assessing its impact.
4. Investigate deaths as potential surveillance failures
CBP should also examine new deaths as they occur and determine whether they happened within sight of a tower or other surveillance technology. And for those that did, the agency should determine why those people weren’t spotted sooner.
Several agents and officials told us that if Border Patrol agents come across the body of someone presumed to have died while crossing into the US, there’s no requirement to check whether that person died near surveillance infrastructure and no process for doing so. At a minimum, that means potentially valuable evidence about the death goes unexamined. It also means that migrant deaths are not routinely treated as possible failures of the virtual wall.
CBP should automatically check every migrant death against its internal database of towers and investigate those that occurred within surveillance range to determine what the system detected and whether agents responded appropriately. Agents already log GPS coordinates when they apprehend a group or encounter footprints, among other events.
Without that check, law enforcement, medical investigators, and families may never learn that someone died near a surveillance tower—and that footage of the moments leading up to the death may exist. CBP typically deletes surveillance footage from the towers after 30 days unless an internal review is opened, which usually happens only for deaths in custody. At a minimum, flagging these cases could preserve footage for those investigating the death and give families a chance to request it.
Such reviews could also expose flaws in the virtual wall itself. Consider one location we identified in New Mexico, where several people died despite being in clear sight of an advanced AI tower. They died within the span of a few months, sometimes just hundreds of feet from one another. Investigating these cases might reveal, for example, that a camera repeatedly failed to detect or identify people in a particular area, or that agents were alerted and simply never responded.
Carrying out these postmortem inquiries would be the only way to answer the question that families, researchers, and volunteers raised most frequently in our investigation into the hundreds of migrants who died near towers: Did the cameras see them, and nobody came? Or did nobody see them at all?
Deep Dive

articles.title: So wird Compliance zum Wachstumstreiber für Enterprise-Sales
articles.text:
Compliance nachhaltig skalieren: Wie du Doppelarbeit bei neuen Anforderungen vermeidest
Und der Fragebogen ist erst der Anfang: Der nächste Kunde verlangt ISO 27001, ein Automotive-Kunde TISAX, ein US-Kunde SOC 2. Je größer die Kunden werden, desto mehr entscheiden schnelle und belastbare Compliance-Nachweise über den Vertriebserfolg.
Was Enterprise-Kunden wirklich prüfen
Security-Fragebögen sehen auf den ersten Blick nach vielen unterschiedlichen Anforderungen aus, drehen sich inhaltlich jedoch meist um dieselben Fragen:
- Wer darf auf welche Systeme zugreifen (Berechtigungskonzept)?
- Welche Dienstleister verarbeiten Daten (Vendor Management)?
- Wie werden Sicherheitsvorfälle behandelt und welche Löschfristen gelten?
- Welche technischen und organisatorischen Maßnahmen (TOMs) sind konkret umgesetzt?
Bei kleineren Deals reicht oft eine Selbstauskunft. Bei Enterprise-Kunden, regulatorischen Vorgaben (wie NIS2, DORA, dem Cyber Resilience Act oder dem EU AI Act) und branchenspezifischen Standards kommen formale Nachweise wie ISO 27001, SOC 2 oder TISAX hinzu.
Der Kunde fragt dabei nach der Kontrolle und dem Nachweis, nicht nach dem spezifischen Framework dahinter. Viele Unternehmen haben deshalb kein neues Compliance-Problem, sondern ein Wiederverwendungsproblem: Wer jedes Framework als separates Projekt behandelt, beschreibt Controls neu, sucht Nachweise erneut zusammen und dokumentiert Verantwortlichkeiten mehrfach.
Die Antworten existieren meist schon, sie sind nur verteilt
Das Problem sind selten die 200 Fragen selbst, sondern dass Antworten im Unternehmen verstreut liegen: Datenschutz bei Legal, ISO 27001 im ISMS, Richtlinien in SharePoint und technische Docs bei der IT.
Dabei überschneiden sich oftmals die Anforderungen. Ein dokumentiertes Berechtigungskonzept oder ein Incident-Prozess lassen sich für nahezu jedes Framework nutzen. Die Skalierungsfrage lautet daher: Wie nutzen wir einmal erarbeitete Controls und Nachweise für möglichst viele Anforderungen?
Compliance-Dokumentation wird zur technischen Schuld
Aus der Softwareentwicklung ist das Muster als „Technical Debt“ bekannt: Gleiche Logik existiert mehrfach, ohne zentrale Quelle. Wird bei Compliance ein Prozess geändert, aber nur an einer Stelle aktualisiert, tauchen beim nächsten Audit widersprüchliche Versionen auf. Das erhöht den Aufwand und gefährdet Audits.
Unternehmen brauchen eine zentrale Quelle (Single Source of Truth):
- Ein Control wird einmal beschrieben.
- Ein Nachweis wird einmal gepflegt.
- Anschließend wird gemappt, welche Framework-Anforderungen damit erfüllt sind.
Kommt ein neues Framework hinzu, prüft man nur noch die Lücken (Gap-Analyse), statt bei null zu beginnen.
Was sich automatisieren lässt und was nicht
Software eignet sich hervorragend für:
- Automatisches Mapping: Verknüpfung von Überschneidungen zwischen Frameworks.
- Reusability: Systemische Wiederverwendung bestehender Controls und Nachweise.
- Gap-Analyse: Schnelle Identifikation fehlender Informationen.
Vollständig automatisieren lässt sich Compliance dennoch nicht. Ob NIS2 oder der Cyber Resilience Act bei komplexen Unternehmensstrukturen greifen oder wie der Scope einer Zertifizierung gezogen werden sollte, erfordert fachliche Bewertung. Software schafft die Struktur und reduziert Routinearbeit – strategische Entscheidungen bleiben Aufgabe von Expert:innen.
Vom Rechercheprojekt zur Unternehmensinfrastruktur
Mit einem zentralen Fundament verändert sich der Vertriebsprozess fundamental: Security-Fragebögen werden von aufwendigen Recherche-Projekten zur einfachen Abfrage vorhandener Daten. Nachweise lassen sich wiederverwenden und neue Frameworks docken nahtlos an. Compliance wird so zum Enabler für schnelles Enterprise-Wachstum.
Wie heyData diesen Ansatz in der Praxis umsetzt
Entscheidend ist, dass geleistete Compliance-Arbeit wiederverwendet werden kann. Genau darauf ist heyData ausgelegt:
- Zentrale Plattform: Bündelt Datenschutz, Informationssicherheit und AI-Governance an einem Ort.
- Multi-Framework-Ansatz: Controls und Nachweise werden einmalig angelegt und flexibel in verschiedenen Frameworks (z. B. ISO 27001, NIS2, DSGVO) zugeordnet.
- Hybrider Ansatz: Wo reine Software an ihre Grenzen stößt, unterstützen Domain-Expert:innen aus Datenschutz, Recht und Informationssicherheit bei Audits und regulatorischen Einordnungen.
Mehr als 2.500 Unternehmen nutzen heyData bereits, um Compliance nicht mehr isoliert pro Framework aufzubauen, sondern auf einem zentralen Fundament zu bündeln.
Vereinbare jetzt deinen unverbindlichen Compliance-Check.

articles.title: SEMICON India 2026 concludes with 15 announcements, headlined by Indian startups and student teams
articles.text:
SEMICON India 2026 concludes with 15 announcements, headlined by Indian startups and student teams
The final day put the spotlight on Indian startups and student teams building on homegrown chip platforms, alongside a new industry report projecting sharp growth for the country's semiconductor market.
New Delhi's Yashobhoomi convention centre wrapped up SEMICON India 2026 on September 19, 2026 with a concluding session that packed in 15 announcements, ranging from indigenous processor challenges to sovereign computing partnerships and skilling tie-ups, according to a press release from the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY).
The day put the spotlight on Indian startups and student teams building on homegrown chip platforms, alongside a new industry report projecting sharp growth for the country's semiconductor market.
SEMICON India 2026, the fifth edition of the event, ran from September 17 to 19 and was jointly organised by the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) and SEMI on the theme 'Silicon to Systems: Building the Ecosystem'.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the conference on its opening day. The event has grown into one of the country's largest semiconductor gatherings, bringing together government bodies, global chipmakers, academic institutions and start-ups as India works to build out design, manufacturing and packaging capabilities under its broader Semicon India programme.
Student teams turn indigenous chips into real products
The clearest entrepreneurial story from the closing session came from the Digital India RISC-V (DIR-V) Grand Challenge, organised by Maker Village under the Chips to Startup Programme of MeitY. The contest drew 1,236 teams comprising 5,045 participants, and three winning teams shared a total prize purse of Rs 60 lakh.
Meevisai Technologies, representing a SASTRA University team, took the first prize for an autonomous water-surface cleaning robot built on the indigenous SHAKTI processor developed by IIT Madras, aimed at cleaning ponds and temple tanks. Digiscope LLP won the second prize for VEGA Chikitsa, a digital stethoscope that captures heart and lung sounds with real-time filtering and machine-learning-assisted murmur screening, built on CDAC's VEGA processor. Zetawave Technologies, an IISc Bengaluru team, took the third prize for a forest-environment monitoring system, also on the VEGA platform.
Startups get investor time, and the market outlook brightens
Startup engagement ran through several other parts of the day. Under Startup Mitra, 11 startups pitched to more than 20 venture capital investors, with Elphins Technologies placing first, Meukron Technologies second, and Multi Nano Sense Technologies and CraftifAI sharing third place. A parallel SEMICON India Hackathon drew 3,808 team registrations from 881 colleges and 1,053 ideas, with 10 teams reaching the grand finale; teams from VIT Vellore and IIT Madras emerged as winners.
Adding context to the day's numbers, EY and the India Semiconductor and Electronics Association launched a report titled 'Semicon India 2.0: From Capacity Creation to Ecosystem Leadership'. The report estimates that India's semiconductor market could grow from nearly $64 billion in 2026 to $200 billion by 2035, and it lays out a roadmap for converting domestic demand and design talent into leadership across manufacturing, advanced packaging and innovation, reports suggest. Beyond the startup track, the session also saw C-DAC launch PARAM Vidya, a plug-and-play AI lab-in-a-box for universities and MSMEs, and PARAM Shavak-QS, a compact quantum simulation platform, alongside partnerships between C-DAC and NLC India, and C-DAC and Bharat Electronics Limited, for sovereign data-centre and computing infrastructure.
What is RISC-V and why India is betting on it
RISC-V is an open, royalty-free processor architecture, meaning any company or research group can design chips on it without paying licensing fees to a proprietary chip-design firm. For India, which has historically depended on foreign architectures for processor design, this matters because it lowers the barrier for home-grown players to build their own chips from the ground up.
That is why platforms like SHAKTI, developed at IIT Madras, and VEGA, developed by CDAC, carry weight beyond the prize money at events such as the DIR-V Grand Challenge. Each winning product built on these processors becomes a small proof point that Indian teams can design and deploy usable hardware on domestically developed silicon, rather than only assembling around imported chips.
Taken together, the concluding session's announcements, layered on top of 41 MoUs and initiatives unveiled during the first two days, point to an event that MeitY is positioning as a bridge between policy intent and on-ground execution. With the EY-ISEA report setting a 2035 horizon for India's semiconductor ambitions, the next test will be whether winning startups such as Meevisai and Digiscope, and the skilling partnerships announced alongside them, can scale from hackathon prototypes and MoUs into deployable products and a trained workforce over the coming years.

articles.title: Xiaomi 18: Price, release date, specs and features guide
articles.text:
Table of contents
Xiaomi has not confirmed the Xiaomi 18, but certification records and fresh leaks already show what the phone could bring. A device widely reported as the global Xiaomi 18 has cleared Taiwan’s regulator after an earlier European filing. This article separates what is confirmed from what is leaked, and shows what it means for you if you plan to buy in Nigeria.
Xiaomi 18 specs at a glance
| Specification | What we know | Status | 
|---|---|---|
| Release date | China launch expected late in 2026, no date yet | Leaked | 
| Display | About 6.4 inches, flat OLED, near 2K resolution | Leaked | 
| Processor | Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6, built on a 2nm process | Leaked | 
| Rear cameras | Possible 200MP periscope camera, full setup unclear | Leaked | 
| Battery | About 7,200mAh; reports range from 7,000 to 7,800mAh | Leaked | 
| Wired charging | Up to 100W | Confirmed | 
| Wireless charging | Expected at 50W | Leaked | 
| Storage | 256GB and 512GB | Confirmed | 
| Water resistance | IP68 | Confirmed | 
| Software | HyperOS 4, likely built on Android 17 | Leaked | 
This table is a snapshot before launch. Xiaomi can change specs between the Chinese and global versions, and certification papers do not show the full retail spec sheet.
Xiaomi 18 release date
Xiaomi has kept the Xiaomi 18 launch date under wraps. Reports say the standard phone will arrive after the Xiaomi 18 Pro models, with a China launch expected toward the end of 2026. Some reports point to December, but treat that as a target rather than a set date.
The proof for a global version is stronger than the proof for a December date. Model number 2611FPNFAG appeared in European certification records in July 2026 and later showed up in Taiwan’s regulator database on September 9. Tech outlets link it to the global Xiaomi 18, though Xiaomi has not confirmed that link.
A certification does not mean Xiaomi will hold one worldwide launch event in December. Regulatory approval often lands weeks or months before a phone goes on sale. It does show that Xiaomi is getting the device ready for Taiwan and possibly other markets outside China.
The rollout could follow the same pattern as the Xiaomi 17. Xiaomi launched that phone in China first, then brought the standard Xiaomi 17 to global buyers at its Barcelona event on February 28, 2026. An early certification could shorten that gap this time, but the final timeline is still unclear.
Xiaomi 18 global and Nigeria availability
There is no confirmed launch country, global sale date, or Nigerian release date yet. The G in model number 2611FPNFAG usually points to a global variant, and both the European and Taiwan filings support an international release. Neither filing guarantees a Nigerian launch.
You may see imported Chinese units before the global model arrives. These units can differ in software, mobile bands, eSIM support, built-in apps, and warranty coverage. A Chinese unit may need extra setup for Google Play, Google Wallet, Android Auto, or certain notifications, and it may support English while limiting other languages and region-specific AI tools.
Check these four things before you pay for an imported Xiaomi 18:
- The exact model number and its supported 4G and 5G bands
- Google service support, plus SIM and eSIM options
- Available languages and the charger type in the box
- Return terms and repair coverage, since a seller warranty is not the same as official local support
Xiaomi 18 price
Xiaomi has not announced a price for the Xiaomi 18, and there is no reliable Nigerian price yet since the phone has not launched anywhere.
The Xiaomi 17 gives the best starting point. It launched in China from CNY 4,499 and later reached Europe from 999 euros for the 12GB/256GB model, with the 12GB/512GB version priced at 1,099 euros. These are prices from the older model, not estimates for the Xiaomi 18.
Xiaomi may try to keep the Xiaomi 18 close to where the Xiaomi 17 sits in its lineup. A move to new 2nm chips, sharper cameras and pricier memory could push the price up. Xiaomi could also offer different storage options in different markets.
A straight currency conversion will not tell you the Nigerian retail price. Imported units carry shipping costs, insurance, customs charges, exchange rate swings, and a seller markup. An official distributor may also set a different regional price.
Detailed specs
1. Design and durability
Leaks describe the Xiaomi 18 as a compact flagship with a flat front and narrow bezels. The display may grow slightly from the Xiaomi 17’s 6.3 inches to about 6.4 inches. Xiaomi has not published the dimensions, weight, frame material, or full colour lineup.
Certification reports list IP68 protection. If this rating makes the final spec sheet, it means the phone resists dust and controlled freshwater immersion under lab conditions. It doesn’t make the phone waterproof in every situation, and liquid-damage terms can vary by warranty.
An ultrasonic in-display fingerprint reader is likely since the Xiaomi 17 already uses one, but Xiaomi has not confirmed it for the Xiaomi 18.
2. Display
Reports point to a flat OLED display measuring roughly 6.3 to 6.4 inches, with near-2K resolution, slim bezels, and an adaptive refresh rate. Xiaomi has not confirmed the exact panel type, pixel count, brightness, or protective glass.
The Xiaomi 17 sets a useful benchmark. Its global model has a 6.3-inch display, a 2656 by 1220 resolution, a 1 to 120Hz adaptive refresh rate, and up to 3,500 nits of claimed peak brightness. You will need official Xiaomi 18 figures before you can call its screen sharper or brighter.
3. Processor and performance
The Xiaomi 18 is widely expected to run Qualcomm’s standard Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 rather than the higher-tier Gen 6 Pro chip reported for the Pro models. The chip is tipped to use TSMC’s 2nm process. Qualcomm has not published the full chip spec sheet as of writing, so its CPU layout, clock speeds, graphics performance, and efficiency gains remain unverified.
This would follow the 3nm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 in the Xiaomi 17, making the Xiaomi 18 one of Xiaomi’s first phones on a Qualcomm 2nm platform. Certification reports list 256GB and 512GB storage with no memory card slot. RAM size, memory type, storage type, and cooling design remain unknown, so treat any early benchmark listing with caution.
4. Cameras
Camera leaks are the least settled part of the Xiaomi 18 story. One report says the standard phone may get a 200MP periscope telephoto camera even without the Pro chip. Other reports describe 200MP sensors across the wider Xiaomi 18 family, sometimes adding a second 200MP main camera and a 50MP ultrawide.
These reports may describe different prototypes, or they may mix up the standard and Pro models. It appears Xiaomi is testing a major zoom upgrade. A final setup of 50MP main, 50MP ultrawide, and 200MP periscope has not been confirmed.
Leica branding is likely since Xiaomi uses Leica optics and imaging modes across its flagship range. The Xiaomi 17 carries three 50MP rear cameras: a main, an ultrawide and a 60mm floating telephoto, plus a 50MP autofocus selfie camera on the global model. The Xiaomi 18’s sensors, apertures, zoom range and video modes remain unknown.
5. Battery and charging
The most repeated battery figure for the Xiaomi 18 sits around 7,200mAh, while wider reports place it between 7,000mAh and 7,800mAh. A silicon-carbon cell could fit that capacity into a fairly compact body, though Xiaomi has not confirmed the number.
Certification coverage supports 100W wired charging. Wireless charging is expected, and 50W shows up often in leak roundups, but the certification does not confirm that figure yet.
Regional capacity matters here. The Chinese Xiaomi 17 uses a 7,000mAh battery, while Xiaomi’s official global spec lists 6,330mAh, and both support 100W wired and 50W wireless charging. Xiaomi could again set different battery sizes by region.
6. Software and AI features
The Xiaomi 18 is expected to ship with HyperOS 4. The global HyperOS 4 beta runs on Android 17, which makes Android 17 the likely base for the phone, though Xiaomi has not confirmed the launch software or update policy.
Reports of a physical AI button tied to Xiaomi’s on-device agent focus mainly on the Xiaomi 18 Pro family, so there isn’t enough evidence to place that button on the standard Xiaomi 18. AI features can also differ by country, language, and software build, so tools shown on a Chinese unit may not appear worldwide.
7. Connectivity
Certification shows an international Xiaomi device moving through approval, but it doesn’t provide a full connectivity list. You can expect 5G, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, NFC, and dual-SIM support. Exact network bands, Wi-Fi version, Bluetooth version, eSIM support, and satellite features remain unknown.
If you plan to import the Chinese version, compare its band list against your network before you buy. A phone can support 5G and still miss a band your operator uses in your area.
Xiaomi 18 vs Xiaomi 17
| Category | Xiaomi 18 | Xiaomi 17 | 
|---|---|---|
| Status | Unannounced, certification and leaks only | Official and on sale in select markets | 
| Display | About 6.4-inch flat OLED, near 2K, leaked | 6.3-inch, 2656 x 1220, 1-120Hz | 
| Processor | Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6, 2nm, leaked | Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5, 3nm | 
| RAM and storage | RAM unknown, 256GB and 512GB reported | 12GB with 256GB or 512GB globally | 
| Rear cameras | Possible 200MP periscope, setup unclear | 50MP main, 50MP ultrawide, 50MP telephoto | 
| Battery | About 7,200mAh, leaked | 7,000mAh China, 6,330mAh global | 
| Wired charging | 100W, from certification | 100W | 
| Wireless charging | 50W expected, unconfirmed | 50W | 
| Software | HyperOS 4 expected | HyperOS 3 at global launch | 
| Water resistance | IP68, from certification | IP68 | 
| Starting price | Unknown | CNY 4,499 China, 999 euros global | 
The Xiaomi 18 column holds pre-launch information only. Xiaomi’s official announcement can change this comparison by a wide margin.
Should you wait for the Xiaomi 18?
Waiting makes sense if you want Xiaomi’s next compact flagship and can hold off until the launch details are clear. The expected 2nm chip, possible 200MP telephoto camera, and bigger battery could bring real gains, and the early certification gives you some reason to expect a global version.
The Xiaomi 17 remains the safer buy today. Its price, cameras, software, battery, and charging are already known, and discounts tend to grow as a new model gets closer. The Xiaomi 18’s December timing, camera setup and battery size are still rumours.
If Google services, Android Auto, network compatibility and warranty matter to you, wait for the exact global model. Buying an early Chinese import can get you the phone faster, but it adds risk around software, network bands, repairs, and the final price you pay.
Your decision also depends on the Xiaomi 18 Pro price. A small gap between the Pro and the standard model could make the Pro the better pick. A bigger gap would strengthen the case for the standard Xiaomi 18 as the more practical compact flagship. Xiaomi’s official launch will settle this.
Xiaomi 18 frequently asked questions
Q) When will the Xiaomi 18 be released?
Xiaomi has not set a date. Reports point to a late 2026 China launch, with December mentioned often. A global date is still unknown.
Q) How much will the phone cost?
There is no official price yet. The phone started at CNY 4,499 in China and 999 euros globally, which gives context rather than a confirmed Xiaomi 18 estimate.
Q) Will the Xiaomi 18 launch globally?
A model widely identified as the global Xiaomi 18 has appeared in European and Taiwanese certification records. This supports an international release, though Xiaomi has not confirmed the markets or date.
Q) Will the Xiaomi 18 come to Nigeria?
Xiaomi has not announced Nigerian availability. Imported units may show up before any official local release.
Q) What processor will the Xiaomi 18 use?
Leaks point to the standard Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6, reportedly built on a 2nm process. Qualcomm and Xiaomi have not confirmed this pairing.
Q) Will the phone have a 200MP camera?
Leaks say the standard model may use a 200MP periscope camera, but the final camera system is still unknown.
Q) How big is the Xiaomi 18 battery?
Reports most often cite about 7,200mAh, with some giving a wider range of 7,000mAh to 7,800mAh. Final capacity may vary by region.
Q) Is the Xiaomi 18 better than the Xiaomi 17?
It may offer a newer chip, a bigger battery, and a stronger zoom camera, but those upgrades remain unconfirmed for now, while the Xiaomi 17 is already documented and on sale.

articles.title: En 2014 descubrimos que el "océano" más grande de la Tierra está enterrado en el subsuelo. Y ahora sabemos por qué
articles.text:
Desde hace años, los expertos saben que en el centro de la Tierra hay agua. Los isótopos llevan más de una década diciéndonos que, allí abajo, queda agua primordial, la que había en el planeta cuando apenas era una bola de magma. El problema es que nadie tenía ni idea de cómo era eso siquiera posible.
Eso acaba de cambiar. Ahora sabemos dónde está la caja fuerte.
Y fuimos bajando poco a poco... En 2014, un equipo de la Universidad Northwestern anunció lo que la prensa tradujo como que "el 'océano' más inmenso de nuestro planeta está bajo tierra". No era exactamente así, claro: lo que habíamos descubierto era que en la zona de transición hay (al menos localmente) en torno a un 1% de agua.
Las pruebas. Un años después, en las lavas de la isla de Baffin, los investigadores descubrieron huellas indelebles de agua que nunca había pasado por la superficie. Y así poco a poco hemos ido encontrando agua cada vez más abajo hasta que, a finales de 2025, se publicó que la bridgmanita pudo retener entre 0,08 y 1 veces el agua de todos los océanos al cristalizar el magma primitivo hace más de 4.000 millones de años.
Es decir, ya solo nos faltaba el último piso.
Y eso precisamente es lo nuevo. Los minerales capaces de secuestrar hidrógeno en posiciones cercanas al núcleo son esquivos; ni los conocemos, ni los entendemos muy bien. Los candidatos que conocíamos tenían serios problemas para ser viables.
Ahora un equipo internacional encabezado por Hongsheng Yuan, del HPSTAR de Shanghái ha descubierto unos 'oxihidróxidos' del hierro que sí pueden hacerlo: son tan densos que, de existir en la Tierra, se hundirían hasta reposar sobre el núcleo; y para formarse les basta con muy poquita agua. Es decir, ahora sabemos cómo y por qué hay agua ahí abajo.
¿Y por qué nos interesa? En el principio, este descubrimiento parece muy teórico. Una curiosidad sin más. Pero tiene más miga de lo que parece: si una parte del agua primigenia ha estado escondida en el manto desde el principio, la habitabilidad de la Tierra nunca ha dependido tanto como creíamos de cometas y asteroides.
Significa que la Tierra siempre tuvo aquello que necesitaba para que nosotros estuviéramos aquí.

articles.title: Noël en septembre : voici les raisons qui forcent les enseignes françaises à remplir leurs rayons trois mois trop tôt
articles.text:
Noël en septembre : voici les raisons qui forcent les enseignes françaises à remplir leurs rayons trois mois trop tôt
Il fait encore doux sur toute la France, avec même 30 degrés dans certaines parties du pays. Et pourtant; les décorations de Noël sont déjà de retour dans les magasins français. Trois mois nous séparent de Noël mais des enseignes comme Action, GiFi ou La Foir’Fouille affichent déjà des sapins, des produits de Noël et autres guirlandes parmi les nouveautés.
Les pays anglophones parlent de "Christmas creep", soit la commercialisation de plus en plus précoce des produits de Noël dans les rayons. La stratégie est simple puisque plus la période de vente commence tôt, plus les enseignes ont le temps d’écouler leurs produits. La méthode existe depuis longtemps mais en France, elle est bien plus visible depuis quelques années. Et il y a aussi le pouvoir d'achat qui entre dans l'équation pour que les consommateurs lissent leurs achatsd e Noël.
Pourquoi on trouve des produits de Noël en septembre ?
La logistique explique ces produits de Noël alors que nous sommes encore loin des fêtes. Les enseignes de bazar commandent certaines collections près d’un an en amont. Puisqu’il s’agit en grande partie d’articles produits en Chine, il faut compter le temps du trajet entre les usines, les ports et les entrepôts, soit plusieurs semaines.
Quand les stocks sont en France, les magasins ont intérêt à les placer rapidement en rayon au lieu de les laisser prendre la poussière dans les réserves pendant plusieurs mois. Et cela libère aussi de la place pour les arrivages suivants. Mais ça ne suffit pas à tout expliquer.
Les clients commencent eux aussi leurs achats de Noël bien plus tôt puisqu’en 2025, une étude PwC montrait que 77 % des Français prévoyaient d’acheter une partie de leurs cadeaux lors du Black Friday. Le budget moyen prévu pour cette période atteint les 231 €.
Bref, le Black Friday est un rendez-vous majeur pour faire ses emplettes de Noël à l’avance, ce qui pousse les enseignes à proposer les produits en amont des fêtes. Et puis il y a aussi le pouvoir d’achat.
En 2025, Cofidis évalue le budget moyen de Noël à 491 € par personne, soit 297 € de cadeaux et 123 € de repas. Depuis 2017, jamais ce budget moyen n’a été aussi bas. L’étude nous explique que 38 % des Français comptent justement profiter des promotions pour acheter les produits de Noël tout en faisant des économies.
La stratégie est simple : échelonner les achats sur plusieurs mois pour éviter une grosse dépense en une seule fois.
Une stratégie pensée par les enseignes
Mais cette stratégie surcharge aussi les rayons puisque chez Action, on trouve des produits d’Halloween qui côtoient ceux de Noël en même temps avec quelques mètres de distance qui séparent les citrouilles des Pères Noël.
Ça n’a que peu de cohérence et on en oublie que les décorations ne sont pas là que pour vendre quelques guirlandes mais posent une ambiance qui rappelle aux clients que les cadeaux, les repas et les fêtes approchent.
Vous l’aurez compris, les décorations de Noël proposées en septembre ne sont pas une erreur de calendrier ou une simple lubie. C’est la réponse à une stratégie précise qui mêle logistique, durée de vente et habitudes d’achat.
Alors jusqu’où le "Christmas creep" ira ? Verrons-nous un jour des produits de Noël dans nos rayons dès l’été, peut-être même en plein juillet alors que les températures côtoient des sommets ?

articles.title: US and China could start warning each other about dangerous AI incidents under new proposal
articles.text:
In brief: The US and China aren't known for cooperating, but the United States wants to work with its rival to implement a safety notification mechanism for AI incidents. The news comes just days after reports that an AI hallucination almost started a war between the two countries.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that the proposal was part of weekend discussions ahead of talks at the White House taking place this week between President Donald Trump and China's Xi Jinping.
Bessent said the two countries had discussed establishing a new US-China AI dialogue, including a system for notifying each other of AI-related incidents with potential national security implications.
"We want a shared vision of common goals and common threats," Bessent said. "We think that just like any cross-border activity, that moving from opaque to more transparency between the No. 1 and the No. 2 AI powers in the world is very important."
Details of how the proposed notification system would operate remain unclear, including which agencies would manage it and what incidents would trigger an alert.
"The fact that both sides agreed to continue the dialogue is significant," George Chen, a partner and chair of digital practice at The Asia Group consultancy, said in written comments (via AP). "The initial outcome – an AI risk notification mechanism – sets a precedent that other countries may follow."
Separately, US and Chinese security experts have called for a dedicated military hotline to prevent accidental or unauthorized AI activity from being mistaken for a deliberate attack, though neither government has publicly endorsed that proposal.
Trump has repeatedly pushed back against any slowdown in AI development, calling safety concerns a "hoax." The president believes the US needs to stay ahead of China in the AI race for both economic and security reasons.
Incidents involving AI agents going rogue have dominated the headlines recently. But a potentially even more dangerous event took place earlier this year involving the military.
Sources say that the US came close to intercepting a Chinese vessel in the Middle East this spring after an AI-assisted intelligence report falsely suggested it was transporting materials for a nuclear weapons program. The claim originated in an inaccurate chatbot response.
According to two sources, armed military personnel were getting ready to board the ship and military aircraft were already airborne when officials reviewed the report more closely and found that AI had generated at least some of its content.

articles.title: Scalpers List Steam Frame Reservations at $1,700+ on eBay, Community Fights Back
articles.text:
Sunday, September 20th 2026
	
									
	
	
	
Scalpers List Steam Frame Reservations at $1,700+ on eBay, Community Fights Back
Scalpers have apparently started listing Steam Frame reservations on eBay within hours of Valve sending its first reservation emails. Per IGN, listings for the 256 GB kit start around $1,700 versus Valve's $1,059, while 1 TB kits are listed at roughly $2,000 versus $1,299. IGN says at least some have already sold, but Mixed points out these are asking prices, and we haven't seen a confirmed sale. Valve's terms seem to work against these listings. The Limited Drop Program terms tie the purchase link to the qualifying Steam account, and they bar transferring the right to buy. No Steam Frame has shipped to a buyer in the US, Canada, the UK, the EU, or Australia, so you would be paying for a place in the queue, not a headset. eBay's policy also requires listings to offer a physical, tangible item.
Perhaps more interestingly, the community is pushing back against these scalpers. Users on r/Steam shared how to report the listings, and one said eBay sent a flood of emails confirming removals. Others found scalpers' Steam usernames in listings and reported them to Valve. We don't know if Valve has acted on any of it, and it also hasn't publicly commented on scalping since the September 14 launch. Valve used the same randomized lottery system for the Steam Machine, which still ended up on eBay regardless. It would be naive to assume that Valve can fully stop this while supply stays tight, but it is nice to see the community mobilize against scalpers.

articles.title: Alibaba Open Sources OpenCodeReview for AI-Assisted Code Review
articles.text:
Alibaba recently open-sourced OpenCodeReview, an AI-powered code review CLI that combines deterministic pipelines for file selection, bundling, and rule matching with an LLM agent for dynamic code analysis. It supports built-in checks for issues such as null-pointer exceptions, thread safety, XSS, and SQL injection.
Open-sourced under an Apache-2.0 license, OpenCodeReview is a Go-based CLI that avoids using AI for decisions that can be handled deterministically, such as selecting files, choosing tools, and validating review comments against the diff. It therefore breaks the review process into multiple stages, each using a different level of determinism: deterministic components handle file selection, bundling, and rule matching, while AI agents perform code analysis.
Reportedly used internally by tens of thousands of Alibaba developers for two years, OpenCodeReview works with OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible models and can review Git diffs, branches, or entire files. Tom Rochette, senior developer at Shopify, reviews the project and writes:
The architecture targets real agent failure modes: incomplete coverage, line-number drift, prompt instability, on large changesets. Ships a public benchmark and transparently discloses its recall disadvantage, which is better evidence behavior than most of the category.
Alibaba states that, in an internal benchmark covering 200 pull requests across 10 languages, OpenCodeReview achieved higher precision and F1 scores than Claude Code while using roughly one-ninth the tokens. Rochette warns:
The one independent benchmark run so far was ugly: about 12 percent precision on 10 Martian-benchmark PRs, disputed by the maintainer as a tool-call anomaly and fixed, with no independent post-fix validation. Recall is deliberately lower than a general agent; teams wanting maximum defect-finding should know that is not this tool's bet.
In the article "OpenCodeReview and the Determinism Dividend," Daniel Vaughan, head of forward deployed engineering at HCLTech, warns about the recall ceiling and AACR-Bench’s scope:
The best configuration achieves 20% recall — meaning 80% of expert-identified issues go unfound. The deterministic dispatch that drives precision also limits discovery of cross-file and architectural issues that require broader exploration.
Early community reactions have focused less on Alibaba's benchmark claims and more on its architecture, particularly the decision to keep file selection, rule matching, and comment positioning deterministic. Vaughan concludes:
OpenCodeReview’s contribution is not a better model but a better harness. By injecting determinism at file dispatch, bounding tool access, and filtering through an independent reflector, it achieves 2.17× the review quality at a fraction of the token cost2.
OpenCodeReview can run locally or integrate with GitHub, GitLab, Gerrit, VS Code, MCP, and coding agents including Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor.

articles.title: Ce TV OLED LG abordable de 2026 qui permet de jouer en 4K 120 Hz voit son prix s'alléger de 200 euros — Frandroid
articles.text:
C’est en mars que LG a présenté sa nouvelle série de téléviseurs OLED B6, conçue pour celles et ceux qui voudraient s’équiper d’un TV OLED sans pour autant dépenser une fortune. La version 55 pouces permet de profiter de contrastes infinis, de jouer en 4K à 120 Hz ou encore de bénéficier d’une compatibilité avec les meilleures normes vidéo, le tout sans avoir à dépenser plus de 1 300 euros grâce à une promotion.
Les points essentiels du TV LG OLED55B65LA
- Une dalle 4K OLED de 55 pouces + 120 Hz
- Quatre ports HDMI 2.1
- webOS 26 et ses cinq ans de mises à jour
Auparavant affiché à 1 499 euros, le TV LG OLED55B65LA est aujourd’hui disponible en promotion à 1 298,99 euros sur le site officiel de LG.
De beaux contrastes et de l’IA pour optimiser chaque image
Le LG OLED55B65LA présente tout d’abord un design particulièrement élégant, avec des bordures si fines qu’elles sont à peine visibles. Un détail qui prend tout son sens lorsque le mode Galerie est activé : le TV affiche alors une œuvre d’art et, grâce aux bords discrets, donne davantage l’impression d’être un véritable tableau accroché au mur. Il se fond donc harmonieusement dans la déco quand il n’est pas utilisé. Mais on le préfère évidemment allumé, avec sa dalle OLED 4K de 55 pouces, qui offre des contrastes infinis et des noirs profonds.
L’écran bénéficie en prime d’un taux de rafraîchissement natif atteignant 120 Hz, ce qui devrait plaire aux gamers et amateurs des matchs de foot. En revanche, le TV étant un modèle OLED d’entrée de gamme, son écran est moins lumineux que celui de ses homologues plus onéreux, mais c’est le prix à payer pour bénéficier d’un tarif plus doux. Le téléviseur est par ailleurs équipé du processeur a8 AI 4K Gen3, qui s’appuie sur l’intelligence artificielle pour améliorer la qualité des images en temps réel, notamment en affinant les détails, les couleurs et les contrastes. Le TV est en prime compatible avec les formats Dolby Vision, HDR10 et HLG.
Côté audio, notons la présence de la fonction AI Sound Pro, qui virtualise un son surround 11.1.2 via les haut-parleurs intégrés, pour renforcer l’immersion. La technologie WOW Orchestra, elle, permet de synchroniser les haut-parleurs d’une barre de son LG compatible avec ceux du téléviseur, pour enrichir la scène sonore.
Un gaming fluide et une bonne réactivité
Ce téléviseur LG est par ailleurs équipé de quatre ports HDMI 2.1 qui permettent de profiter d’un affichage en 4K jusqu’à 120 Hz. Les joueurs disposant d’une configuration suffisamment puissante peuvent ainsi bénéficier d’un affichage particulièrement fluide et détaillé. Évidemment, on peut également brancher des consoles de dernière génération comme la PS5 et la Xbox Series X, qui plafonnent elles aussi à 120 Hz. Notez que les prises prennent également en charge les technologies ALLM et VRR, lesquelles optimisent l’expérience en réduisant le délai d’affichage et en limitant les saccades et les déchirures d’image. La compatibilité Nvidia G-Sync et AMD FreeSync Premium est aussi de la partie.
Enfin, ce TV fonctionne sous webOS 26 et bénéficie depuis sa sortie du programme webOS Re:New, qui lui garantit jusqu’à cinq ans de mises à jour majeures de l’interface. Vous avez aussi accès à un Home Hub, qui centralise les appareils connectés compatibles de votre domicile et vous permet de les piloter plus facilement depuis le téléviseur.
Si vous souhaitez découvrir d’autres modèles de la marque, nous vous invitons dès maintenant à consulter notre guide des meilleurs TV LG du moment.

articles.title: Tiene 10 episodios y es la serie de ciencia ficción más rara de Movistar+
articles.text:
La ciencia ficción suele ser sorprendente y por una razón. No deja de imaginar el mundo de las maneras más raras y curiosas posibles. Por lo que el género puede presumir que es capaz de indagar en todos los aspectos de la vida del ser humano desde lugares curiosos. Que es precisamente lo que ocurre con La mujer miniatura, una fascinante y demencial visión sobre la convivencia y el amor. Pero claro, desde el punto de vista de la ciencia ficción pura, con todo lo que eso supone. Incluyendo una perspectiva delirante de la naturaleza humana.
Por lo que la serie de ciencia ficción combina de manera brillante elementos del género, comedia romántica y drama psicológico. Pero además, analizar la idea sobre cosas un poco más sutiles como las relaciones de poder en las relaciones y hasta el desencanto. Todo mientras sigue a una pareja que debe enfrentar lo inimaginable. Debido a un experimento científico fallido de su marido, una mujer termina por ser reducida hasta volverse tan pequeña como una muñeca. Pero lo que parece una premisa burlona (lo es en cierta forma), pronto se convierte en una idea más retorcida. En especial, porque en este caso, el tamaño de la protagonista es la forma de entender varias cosas a la vez.
Desde la dependencia psicológica, el miedo al futuro hasta la búsqueda de propósito. La mujer miniatura va de un lado a otro de varios tropos de la ciencia ficción para contar una idea básica. La raza humana debe luchar contra sus propias mezquindades. Adaptación del relato corto de 2013 escrito por el autor Manuel Gonzales, La mujer miniatura explora el desgaste matrimonial a través de una lente fantástica. Por lo que la serie usa su insólita historia para indagar en las relaciones contemporáneas. En especial, los desequilibrios cotidianos se transforman en una lucha literal por la supervivencia física y emocional.
Date de alta en Movistar Plus+ y disfruta de lo mejor del deporte, fútbol, cine, series internacionales, y más de 80 canales. No tiene permanencia e incluye dos reproducciones simultáneas, desde smartphone, TV, PC o Tablet.
Una mujer que intenta sobrevivir desde el punto de la ciencia ficción
Para eso, esta serie de ciencia ficción sigue a Lindy Littlejohn (Elizabeth Banks), una reconocida autora de bestsellers. Una mujer que, además, lidia con un matrimonio infeliz con Les Littlejohn (Matthew Macfadyen). Este, un científico que intenta superar su fracaso en un mecanismo capaz de encoger a cualquiera a una décima de su tamaño. Pero en realidad, el proceso sí funciona y lo comprobará de la manera más alarmante. Lindy terminará encogida accidentalmente hasta medir apenas 15 centímetros. Todo debido a una prueba fallida del misterioso mecanismo.
Para Les es un triunfo luego de años de fracaso. Pero hay un problema. No sabe cómo restaurar a la Lindy a su tamaño normal porque nunca se planteó algo semejante. De hecho, todo su esfuerzo estaba en un sistema de miniaturización que optimizara procesos agrícolas, por lo que no había motivos para revertirlo. Así que tendrá que intentar por todos los medios a su alcance tratar de no encontrar cómo resolver el dilema de agrandar a Lindy. También, hacerlo en un período de tiempo cortísimo. En cuestión de semanas, el proceso será irreversible.
Pero mientras toda esta historia de ciencia ficción pura ocurre, Lindy y Les tendrán que enfrentar algo más. Tras el terrible accidente doméstico, la enorme diferencia de tamaño altera drásticamente la realidad de la pareja. Obligada a habitar en una casa de muñecas modificada para subsistir, Lindy debe aprender a interactuar con un entorno inevitablemente peligroso. Uno donde las cosas más simples y cotidianas de un hogar ordinario representan amenazas mortales. Desde insectos comunes hasta objetos de cocina mal colocados, todo se vuelve un reto logístico mientras intenta asimilar su nueva y reducida condición biológica.
Miedo, terror y matrimonio desde el punto de vista de la ciencia ficción
Por lo que, mientras Lindy batalla por sobrevivir y Les por crear un segundo invento revolucionario, ambos batallan en una tensa batalla psicológica. En específico, el cambio en la dinámica de poder del matrimonio. Antes del incidente, la relación ya sufría por condescendencia y los reclamos mutuos de insatisfacción personal. Pero una vez que Lindy queda físicamente vulnerable y dependiente de las acciones de su marido, todo se vuelve peor. Algo que desencadena un rasgo pérfido y cruel en Les, que Lindy tendrá que conocer y vencer para salvar la vida.
Sin embargo, lejos de sumirse en la sumisión, la protagonista utiliza su astucia e intelecto de escritora para desafiar la autoridad de Les. De modo que convierte el espacio doméstico en un tablero de ajedrez donde ambos cónyuges se disputan la supremacía del hogar. Así que esta serie de ciencia ficción expone cómo el resentimiento puede florecer cuando uno de los miembros de la pareja adquiere una ventaja física. O peor aún, cuando convierte al otro en un enemigo a vencer.
Rara, impredecible y con un final que te dejará desconcertado, La mujer miniatura es mucho más que una serie de ciencia ficción. También es una astuta visión sobre el rencor, el desamor y la violencia doméstica. Todo bajo la apariencia de una situación imposible e inimaginable. Su punto más alto y que demuestra que el género siempre será capaz de explorar en nuestro mundo de la manera más insólita posible. Su mejor rasgo.

articles.title: TCL A1 Plus: tablet com tela grande, teclado físico e caneta compensa? Confira nossa análise
articles.text:
Tablets com caneta são especialmente úteis para quem precisa fazer anotações diretamente na tela, mas o tamanho do display também faz diferença: modelos maiores oferecem mais espaço para escrever e desenhar, enquanto os menores podem exibir informações espremidas e em baixa resolução. E quando o pacote inclui também um teclado, as possibilidades de uso se ampliam.
O Olhar Digital preparou uma análise do TCL A1 Plus, um tablet com tela de 12,2 polegadas que já vem na caixa com uma caneta para anotações diretamente na tela e um teclado para quem quer digitar textos completos nele. Confira abaixo as principais características do modelo:
TCL A1 Plus: ficha técnica
- Tela de 12,2 polegadas 2.4K de 120 Hz
- Processador Snapdragon 4 Gen 2
- 6 GB de RAM e 128 GB de armazenamento (expansível até 2 TB)
- Bateria de 8.000 mAh com recarga de 20 W
- Câmera traseira de 8 MP e frontal de 5 MP
- Android 16 com recursos de IA (Google Gemini e Circule para Pesquisar)
Como é o TCL A1 Plus
O TCL A1 Plus tem o corpo construído em alumínio, com 6,7 milímetros de espessura, pesando 540 gramas. No geral, ele tem dimensões adequadas para um aparelho de 12,2 polegadas, e você consegue segurar o dispositivo com conforto para ler artigos ou assistir a vídeos sem cansar as mãos rapidamente. Ele ainda tem um bom peso e tamanho para ser levado com facilidade em bolsas e mochilas.
O corpo do tablet ainda tem proteção IP54, garantindo resistência a poeira e respingos de água. As bordas ao redor do display são bem perceptíveis, mas não chegam a incomodar durante o uso. Os botões de volume e liga/desliga ficam na parte superior do aparelho quando ele está no modo paisagem, com o conector USB-C e os alto-falantes nas laterais.
A tela de 12,2 polegadas tem tecnologia IPS LCD com resolução 2.4K (2400 x 1600 pixels) com taxa de atualização de 120 Hz e brilho máximo de 550 nits, podendo ser usada em locais iluminados sem perder a visibilidade do conteúdo. A tela tem um formato um pouco diferente de outros modelos que rodam Android, vindo na proporção 3:2, o que acaba sendo bastante útil na leitura de sites, livros e documentos.
Como é usar o TCL A1 Plus
Por dentro, a TCL equipou o A1 Plus com o processador Snapdragon 4 Gen 2 da Qualcomm, aliado a 6 GB de memória RAM e 128 GB de armazenamento interno. A RAM pode ser expandida para 16 GB com uso do modo de RAM virtual, que pega um pouco do armazenamento emprestado para oferecer mais memória para lidar com as tarefas. O espaço interno também pode ser ampliado com uso de cartão de memória micro SD (até 2 TB).
No geral, é um tablet bastante competente, lidando com uso básico para navegação em sites, redes sociais e serviços de streaming sem engasgos. O conjunto de hardware consegue até mesmo lidar com algumas tarefas mais exigentes. Usando o modo de RAM virtual, ele consegue até rodar alguns jogos pesados com gráficos no nível médio sem travamentos.
Um dos destaques do pacote é a inclusão tanto de uma capa protetora com teclado físico quanto da caneta T Pen. Isso faz dele um tablet bastante versátil, podendo ser usado quase como um notebook sem que você precise gastar além do preço inicial. O Android embarcado é a versão 16, que lida muito bem com multitarefa e permite o uso de dois aplicativos lado a lado, janelas flutuantes e um modo que simula uma área de trabalho como a de computadores convencionais.
Ele pode, portanto, ser um simples tablet para lazer, ao navegar em redes sociais e serviços de streaming, como também pode ajudar nos estudos e no trabalho quando usado em conjunto com o teclado físico para digitação de textos mais pesados e com a caneta, para anotações feitas diretamente na tela.
Tablets não costumam ser dispositivos com câmeras muito potentes para usuários exigentes, e o TCL A1 Plus não foge à regra. O sensor traseiro tem 8 megapixels com foco automático e flash LED, enquanto o frontal tem 5 MP.
No geral, as câmeras dão conta de tarefas básicas, como videochamadas e digitalização de documentos, mas definitivamente não são câmeras para quem quer fotos de alta qualidade, ou produção de conteúdo em vídeo para redes sociais.
Com uma bateria de 8.000 mAh, ele aguenta um dia inteiro de uso intenso. A recarga aceita potência de até 20 W e pode ser um pouco demorada: do zero aos 100% ele exige cerca de 2,5 horas a 3 horas conectado à tomada.
O TCL A1 Plus vale a pena?
Um tablet com tela grande, boa bateria e que vem em um pacote completo: o TCL A1 Plus é uma excelente escolha para quem quer um dispositivo que faça mais do que o básico, mas sem precisar pagar o exigido pelos modelos premium. Ele pode não rodar games exigentes com gráficos de ponta, mas dá conta muito bem de tarefas básicas e moderadas.
O fato de acompanhar teclado e caneta torna o pacote ainda mais atrativo, já que você pode usá-lo para estudos e produtividade sem precisar gastar mais do que o preço inicial.
Mas é importante ressaltar algumas das suas fraquezas: o carregamento lento pode prender o usuário por horas próximo a uma tomada para ter energia, e a porta USB-C não tem saída de vídeo, impedindo o uso com monitores externos.

articles.title: Gemini a piraté trois entreprises mais Google ne parle pas de « désalignement »
articles.text:
Vendredi 18 septembre, le Wall Street Journal révélait qu’un modèle Gemini avait accédé à internet en mai, pendant un test de ses capacités en cybersécurité, et s’était introduit dans les systèmes d’autres entreprises.
Pour le quotidien américain, il s’agit du « premier exemple connu où une IA de Google commet de sa propre initiative ce type d’intrusion », alors qu’OpenAI, Anthropic ou encore Meta avaient déjà communiqué sur des incidents comparables.
Reste que le ton adopté par Google, qui a confirmé les faits, est nettement plus mesuré.
Un test, un prestataire, trois entreprises
Selon le Wall Street Journal, ces piratages ont eu lieu lors d’un exercice de « capture the flag » mené par Irregular, une société indépendante qui évalue la sécurité des modèles d’IA.
Gemini a trouvé des informations publiques en ligne et deviné des identifiants pour se connecter à des sites qu’il croyait faire partie de l’exercice, en essayant notamment des mots de passe jusqu’à accéder à un système protégé. Sauf que ces sites appartenaient en réalité à trois entreprises étrangères au test. Interrogé sur le sujet, Heather Adkins, vice-présidente de l’ingénierie de sécurité chez Google, précise que, dans chacun des cas, « le modèle s’est arrêté ».
Pas grand-chose de plus à ce stade, les trois entreprises ne sont pas nommées, on ignore quelles données Gemini a pu consulter, combien d’agents et de tentatives ont été nécessaires, et comment le modèle « s’est arrêté ».
Google insiste davantage sur le fait que l’incident s’explique par un accès Internet laissé ouvert par Irregular pendant les tests. Le prestataire indique avoir informé Google et toutes les entités concernées en juillet, et avoir corrigé de son côté les problèmes connus.
Google écarte le désalignement
Contrairement à OpenAI et Anthropic, Google n’a pas accompagné sa confirmation d’un billet de blog détaillé. Selon le Wall Street Journal, le groupe ne jugeait pas la divulgation nécessaire, aucun dommage n’ayant été causé. Il écarte aussi l’idée d’un désalignement (c’est-à-dire d’un modèle qui s’écarte de ce que ses concepteurs attendent de lui) : Gemini s’est arrêté dès qu’il a compris qu’il était chez de vraies entreprises.
Une définition que chaque laboratoire semble désormais employer à sa façon.
Le cas de Gemini se rapproche de celui d’Anthropic. Le modèle a bien exécuté la tâche qui lui était assignée mais s’est trompé sur son environnement. Chez OpenAI, les modèles avaient pour objectif de réussir un benchmark, et y sont arrivés en trichant, par un chemin que personne n’avait prévu.
Le terme n’a pas, pour l’heure, de définition juridique, mais des références existent. Le rapport international sur la sécurité de l’IA qualifie de « désaligné » un système qui tend à adopter des comportements en conflit avec les intentions de ses concepteurs, de ses utilisateurs ou de la société, sans supposer que le modèle ait conscience de l’écart. Celle de Google DeepMind, dans son document sur la sécurité de l’AGI, est plus étroite : le modèle doit causer un tort en connaissance de cause, contre l’intention de ses concepteurs. Un modèle qui croyait agir dans le cadre d’un test s’y range difficilement, alors que la définition large pourrait couvrir le cas d’OpenAI.

articles.title: 3 películas modernas e infravaloradas sobre la Segunda Guerra Mundial que deberías ver
articles.text:
El cine sobre la Segunda Guerra Mundial siempre nos ha dejado grandes películas. El mayor conflicto bélico de la historia de la humanidad se convirtió irremediablemente en uno de los temas más interesantes para plasmar en la gran pantalla. Los ejemplos se cuentan por decenas, ya sea en clásicos como La gran evasión, El día más largo o Casablanca, pasando por obras maestras como La lista de Schindler, Salvar al soldado Ryan, El pianista o La vida es bella, e incluso filmes animados como La tumba de las luciérnagas.
La producción de películas sobre la Segunda Guerra Mundial nunca ha parado y prácticamente cada año llega una o varias cintas que se ganan su hueco entre los espectadores. Solo en esta última década podemos encontrar obras de la talla de Oppenheimer, La zona de interés e incluso la película de los Peaky Blinders: El hombre inmortal.
Evidentemente, no siempre es fácil que estas películas logren convertirse en antemporales. La sobresaturación de estrenos en cine y televisión hace que cada vez sea más complicado resultar relevante. Por eso, a continuación recogemos 3 películas modernas sobre la Segunda Guerra Mundial que merecen no ser olvidadas. Son tres dramas que se alejan del campo de batalla para darnos una visión de lo que sucedía entre bambalinas, en los despachos y oficinas de las mentes más estrategas de la época.
El arma del engaño (2021)
El arma del engaño, estrenada en 2021, es un sensacional drama bélico que nos mete en las entrañas de la Operación Carne Picada. Este plan británico pasaba por emplear un cadáver con documentación falsa para engañar a los nazis haciéndoles creer que los Aliados iban a invadir Grecia, cuando el objetivo real era Sicilia. Bajo la dirección del gran John Madden (Shakespeare enamorado), cuenta con las actuaciones estelares de Colin Firth, Matthew Macfadyen y Kelly MacDonald, entre otros. Mantiene muy bien el pulso, es profunda y está perfectamente contada. Merece mucho la pena.
El arma del engaño está disponible para alquiler en las principales plataformas digitales.
Núremberg (2025)
Núremberg se convirtió en una de las grandes sorpresas de 2025. La película gustó mucho en festivales y el público salió encantado, aunque finalmente no logró hacerse un hueco en los grandes premios. En cualquier caso, la cinta nos regaló una de las mejores interpretaciones de la carrera de Russell Crowe. El oscarizado actor dio vida al político y militar alemán Hermann Göring. Capturado por los Aliados, este líder nazi es analizado por el psiquiatra estadounidense Douglas Kelley (Rami Malek), que debe tratar de entender el por qué de sus viles acciones en el Holocausto de cara a los conocidos Juicios de Núremberg. El duelo psicológico entre ellos es, sencillamente, brutal.
Núremberg está disponible en Movistar Plus+.
Tiempo de victoria (2026)
Cerramos esta lista de películas de la Segunda Guerra Mundial con el estreno más reciente, Tiempo de Victoria. Protagonizada por Andrew Scott y Brendan Fraser, la cinta nos sumerge en los instantes previos al Día D. El meteorólogo James Stagg recibe el encargo de elaborar el pronóstico del parte meteorológico para el día del ataque de los Aliados. Una previsión que puede suponer la diferencia total entre ganar o perder la guerra. Con todos los recursos posibles a su disposición, deberá informar al general Dwight D. Eisenhower sobre si el asedio a Normandía es viable o no.
Tiempo de Victoria está en cines.

articles.title: Keine nervige Suche mehr: So spart dir Gmail jetzt Zeit bei Einmalcodes
articles.text:
Neue Gmail-Funktion: So sparst du jetzt Zeit bei Einmalcodes
Erst vor wenigen Wochen hat Google ein Downgrade für Gmail angekündigt. Ab 2027 wird die „Senden als“-Funktion nicht mehr so funktionieren, wie es User:innen gewohnt sind. Jetzt gibt es aber etwas erfreulichere Nachrichten für alle, die Gmail als Hauptanwendung für Mails nutzen. Denn Google verpasst der App unter iOS und Android eine praktische Funktion, mit der du Zeit sparen kannst.
Einmalcodes in Gmail: So findest du sie jetzt schneller
Wie Android Police berichtet, erkennt Gmail jetzt automatisch, dass eine Mail einen Einmalcode enthält. Das ist etwa der Fall, wenn du 2FA bei einem Dienst aktiviert hast und dich per E-Mail-Code beim Login zusätzlich verifizieren musst. Zahlreiche Dienste nutzen solche Einmalcodes aber auch beim ersten Anmelden. Bisher musstest du die Mails in Gmail immer nach dem Code durchsuchen, markieren und kopieren.
Jetzt scannt Gmail die Nachricht nach dem Code und packt ihn anschließend direkt unter die Betreffzeile in deinem Posteingang. Dort findet sich unter dem Betreff jetzt eine Schaltfläche mit „Code kopieren“. Dadurch landet der Einmalcode in deiner Zwischenablage und du kannst ihn direkt in anderen Apps und im Browser einfügen.
Gmail holt den Code aber auch in der Mail selbst aus dem Text und packt ihn direkt unter den Betreff. Dort wird er nicht nur groß angezeigt, damit er sich einfacher lesen und markieren lässt. Gmail bietet auch hier eine eigene Schaltfläche, um den Code mit einem Antippen zu kopieren. Ein händisches Markieren und Kopieren innerhalb der Mail ist nicht mehr nötig.
Laut Android Police gibt es mit dem Feature aktuell noch kleinere Probleme. Manchmal taucht der Kopieren-Button nicht im Postfach auf, sondern nur in der Mail selbst. Das könnte daran liegen, wie die jeweiligen Absender:innen ihre Mails formatieren. Denkbar wäre, dass Google hier künftig noch nachbessert. Die Neuerung sollte in den kommenden Tagen für alle Gmail-User:innen auf Mobilgeräten ausrollen. Allerdings müssen Web-Nutzer:innen wohl vorerst darauf verzichten. Dort ist das Gmail-Feature bisher nicht zu finden.
