articles.title: Egypt’s Bekia raises $765k to scale recycling economy tech - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Egyptian startup Bekia, which is digitising waste collection, has raised a US$765,000 seed round to deepen its consumer app and launch its first B2B software product.
Founded in 2019, Bekia is a digital platform building the collection layer for Egypt’s recycling economy. The platform began with a consumer app – a household books a pickup, a collector arrives at a scheduled time, material is weighed on the spot at a published rate, and payment goes to a bank account or digital wallet.
At the end of October, Bekia will launch Bekia Next, which turns that data into verified CO₂-avoidance certificates for corporate clients using established international carbon accounting methodology. It is the first thing Bekia sells as a subscription rather than a service.
The startup’s US$765,000 funding round is led by Madica, the Africa-focused investment programme affiliated with Flourish Ventures, and also features Catalyst Fund and Dakar-based Jambaar Capital. Bekia will use the funding to grow its engineering team, take Bekia Next to market, and begin testing the model in a second African market.
“Egypt’s recycling sector has always worked — it just worked invisibly, on cash and trust, with no record of any of it,” said Alaa Afifi, founder and CEO of Bekia. “We built the software layer that changes that: a collector gets a transaction history, a factory gets traceable supply, a household learns what its waste is actually worth. The material itself is a commodity, but the record of it isn’t, and nobody in our market owns that record yet.”
“What excites us about Bekia is how the team is drawing on its firsthand understanding of waste collection in Egypt to build a more interconnected, tech-driven ecosystem serving households, small businesses and large industrial waste producers,” said Emmanuel Adegboye, head of Madica. “We’re proud to welcome them to the Madica programme and support that ambition with long-term capital, company-building expertise and networks.”

articles.title: Xiaomi 18 Pro: Price, release date, specs and features
articles.text:
Table of contents
Xiaomi will unveil the Xiaomi 18 Pro in China on September 23, 2026. The compact flagship is expected to retain the rear display introduced on the Xiaomi 17 Pro, while leaks point to a new 2nm Snapdragon chip, two 200MP cameras, and a battery approaching 7,000mAh.
Some of these details remain unconfirmed ahead of the launch. This guide separates Xiaomi’s confirmed announcements from reported specifications and leaks, so you know what to expect from the Xiaomi 18 Pro.
Xiaomi 18 Pro release date
Xiaomi will hold its autumn launch event on September 23, 2026, at 7 p.m. China time. That works out to 12 p.m. in Nigeria, 7 a.m. Eastern Time, and 4 a.m. Pacific Time.
The event is part of Qualcomm’s Snapdragon Summit, which runs from September 22 to 24 in Maui. Qualcomm is teasing two new Snapdragon 8 Elite platforms for the summit, which makes Xiaomi’s timing significant. Xiaomi has not said when the phone goes on sale after the event.
Will the Xiaomi 18 Pro launch globally?
Xiaomi has only confirmed the Chinese launch. The company has not announced a global release date or named any international markets for the Xiaomi 18 Pro.
This matters because the Xiaomi 17 Pro and 17 Pro Max were limited to China, while Xiaomi later brought the standard Xiaomi 17 and Xiaomi 17 Ultra to international markets. So far, there is no confirmation that the Xiaomi 18 Pro will get an official global release. Importers may still sell the Chinese model in other markets, even if Xiaomi does not launch it internationally.
Xiaomi 18 Pro price
Xiaomi has not announced the Xiaomi 18 Pro price yet. The best guide is the previous model. The Xiaomi 17 Pro launched in China at CNY 4,999 for 12GB of RAM and 256GB of storage.
| Xiaomi 17 Pro configuration | China launch price | 
|---|---|
| 12GB + 256GB | CNY 4,999 | 
| 12GB + 512GB | CNY 5,299 | 
| 16GB + 512GB | CNY 5,599 | 
| 16GB + 1TB | CNY 5,999 | 
Reports expect the Xiaomi 18 Pro to cost at least as much as its predecessor. Higher memory and component costs could push the starting price up. No reliable Nigerian or global price is available yet, and a direct currency conversion would skip shipping, customs charges, retailer margins, and warranty costs.
Xiaomi 18 Pro specs at a glance
| Feature | Reported detail | Status | 
|---|---|---|
| Launch | September 23, 2026, in China | Confirmed | 
| Main display | About 6.3 inches, flat OLED | Leaked | 
| Rear display | Interactive screen built into the camera area | Design confirmed, functions unconfirmed | 
| Processor | Next Snapdragon 8 Elite chip on a reported 2nm process | Expected | 
| RAM and storage | Not announced | Unknown | 
| Rear cameras | Leica system, 200MP main and 200MP telephoto reported | Branding confirmed, resolution leaked | 
| Battery | About 7,000mAh | Leaked | 
| Charging | 100W wired and wireless charging | Leaked | 
| Software | HyperOS 4 based on Android 17 | Expected | 
| Protection | IP68 expected | Unconfirmed | 
Detailed specs
1. Design and rear display
Xiaomi’s official teaser confirms the return of the rear display. It stretches across the camera area, with two camera lenses on the screen and a third lens below. The phone also shows an extra side button that the Xiaomi 17 Pro lacked.
Xiaomi calls this a versatile rear screen. Reports say it supports AI-generated mini-apps, such as an egg timer and a water reminder. Xiaomi’s global website does not fully document these tools yet, so treat them as reported features until the launch event.
Leaks also describe a dedicated AI key. A single press opens Xiaomi’s AI assistant. A double press or long press may control Xiaomi vehicles or smart home routines. The button appears in promotional images, but Xiaomi has not confirmed every shortcut. Reports also mention a dark red finish alongside more familiar colours.
2. Display
The Xiaomi 18 Pro stays a compact flagship with a flat display near 6.3 inches. That keeps it close to the Xiaomi 17 Pro, which also used a 6.3-inch main screen.
Reports link the phone to TCL CSOT’s M11 Super Pixel Real RGB OLED technology. This could improve sharpness and power efficiency through a full RGB subpixel layout. Xiaomi has not confirmed the resolution, refresh rate, peak brightness, or protective glass. Drop the earlier 0.99mm bezel figure, since it cannot be tied reliably to the Xiaomi 18 Pro yet.
3. Chipset and performance
The Xiaomi 18 Pro likely uses one of Qualcomm’s next Snapdragon 8 Elite processors. Qualcomm confirms its coming flagship platform includes an Oryon CPU that reaches 5GHz, but it has not named the final chip for this phone.
A Geekbench listing for a Xiaomi device called M610BB shows Android 17, about 16GB of RAM, and an eight-core Qualcomm processor with two cores reaching 5.01GHz. Treat this as supporting evidence rather than final confirmation, since benchmark listings can change and this model has no official link to the retail Xiaomi 18 Pro yet.
Leaks point to a 2nm manufacturing process. A smaller process should improve performance and efficiency, but actual battery life and sustained gaming performance depend on Xiaomi’s cooling system and software tuning.
4. Cameras
Xiaomi’s images show a Leica-branded triple-camera system, continuing the company’s imaging partnership with Leica.
The biggest rumour points to a pair of 200MP cameras, one main camera and one periscope telephoto camera with macro support. A third camera likely handles ultrawide shots, though its resolution stays unknown. This marks a big change from the Xiaomi 17 Pro, which used three 50MP rear cameras.
Megapixel count alone won’t determine image quality. Sensor size, lens quality, optical zoom, and low-light performance matter just as much. Xiaomi still needs to confirm the sensors, apertures, focal lengths, and video modes.
5. Battery and charging
The most repeated leak puts the Xiaomi 18 Pro at around 7,000mAh, up from the Xiaomi 17 Pro’s 6,300mAh cell. Some later reports mention a capacity as high as 8,000mAh, so the final number remains uncertain.
Reports also say the phone supports 100W wired charging and wireless charging. The Xiaomi 17 Pro supported 100W wired and 50W wireless charging, making similar support likely. Xiaomi has not confirmed the charging speeds or whether the box includes a charger.
6. Software and AI
The Xiaomi 18 Pro should ship with HyperOS 4 based on Android 17 in China. Xiaomi has already released Android 17 developer software and started expanding HyperOS 4 testing, making this combination likely for a late-2026 flagship.
AI sits at the centre of the phone’s pitch. Beyond the rear screen mini-apps, reports point to deeper ties with Xiaomi’s system assistant, device controls, and connected products. Some of these services may stay limited to China. A future global model could use different AI services and features.
7. Memory, storage and cooling
Xiaomi has not announced the RAM or storage options yet. The Xiaomi 17 Pro offered 12GB or 16GB of RAM and up to 1TB of storage, so expect similar configurations. The memory type, storage standard, and cooling hardware stay unknown for now.
8. Connectivity and durability
Expect 5G, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, NFC, and dual-SIM support on a flagship in this class. Xiaomi has not published the exact versions or supported network bands. IP68 water and dust resistance also looks likely, since the Xiaomi 17 Pro carried an IP68 rating, but Xiaomi has not confirmed the new phone’s protection level.
Xiaomi 18 Pro vs Xiaomi 17 Pro
| Feature | Xiaomi 17 Pro | Xiaomi 18 Pro | 
|---|---|---|
| Launch price | From CNY 4,999 | Unannounced, expected near or above CNY 4,999 | 
| Main display | 6.3-inch LTPO AMOLED | About 6.3-inch flat OLED, reported | 
| Rear display | Rear AMOLED screen | Redesigned rear screen with more AI functions | 
| Processor | Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 | Next Snapdragon 8 Elite platform, expected | 
| RAM and storage | 12GB or 16GB, up to 1TB | Unannounced | 
| Rear cameras | Three 50MP cameras | 200MP main and 200MP telephoto reported, third camera unknown | 
| Battery | 6,300mAh | About 7,000mAh reported | 
| Charging | 100W wired, 50W wireless | 100W wired and wireless charging reported | 
| Software at launch | HyperOS 3 on Android 16 | HyperOS 4 on Android 17 expected | 
| Water resistance | IP68 | IP68 expected, unconfirmed | 
Xiaomi 18 Pro in Nigeria
Xiaomi has not announced the Xiaomi 18 Pro for Nigeria. If it stays exclusive to China, you will need to use importers or international marketplaces to get one.
An imported Chinese model may cost far more than a direct price conversion suggests. You pay for shipping, customs clearance, exchange rate changes, and a seller’s markup. Warranty support can also get complicated. Xiaomi Nigeria offers local support and information on international warranty service, but eligibility depends on the device and market. Confirm coverage with Xiaomi before you pay.
Network compatibility raises another concern. A Chinese model may skip frequency bands used outside China. Check the exact model number and its 4G and 5G bands against your network before you order. Also confirm Google Play support, Android Auto compatibility, notification behaviour, and language options.
Should you buy the Xiaomi 18 Pro?
The Xiaomi 18 Pro suits you if you want a compact Android flagship with a large battery, a distinctive rear display, and ambitious camera hardware. It also appeals to you if you already use Xiaomi smart home products or a Xiaomi vehicle.
If you own a Xiaomi 17 Pro, wait for the full camera, battery, and AI demonstrations. The rear screen is similar tothe main design upgrade, while the practical value of the leaked AI tools remains unclear.
If you live in Nigeria, wait for Xiaomi to confirm the price, supported network bands, and international availability. Importing the Chinese version before those details settle brings software, warranty, and connectivity risks.
Xiaomi reveals the remaining specs on September 23. Check back after the event for the official price, complete camera system, battery capacity, charging speeds, memory options, and first sale date.

articles.title: Pourquoi BYD peut vendre ses voitures moins cher que tout le monde, sa stratégie n’est pas facile à reproduire
articles.text:
Pourquoi BYD peut vendre ses voitures moins cher que tout le monde, sa stratégie n’est pas facile à reproduire
On le sait, une grosse partie du succès de BYD repose sur sa politique tarifaire agressive. Mais comment le constructeur chinois arrive à proposer des voitures électriques aussi peu chères ? On a la réponse après démontage d'un SUV électrique Atto 3.
BYD intrigue jusque chez les ingénieurs japonais. Pour mieux saisir comment le constructeur chinois réduit ses coûts à ce point, des spécialistes ont démonté puis étudié son SUV Atto 3. Et le constat est sans appel : la stratégie industrielle de BYD est très différente de celle des constructeurs historiques. L’entreprise produit beaucoup de pièces en interne et son architecture est pensée pour simplifier la fabrication des véhicules.
BYD produit énormément de ses composants
C’est l’antenne régionale du ministère japonais de l’Économie pour le Chubu qui a rassemblé près de 70 équipementiers automobiles dans un centre d’études à Mizunami. Là-bas, on trouvait plusieurs véhicules électriques démontés, parmi lesquels le BYD Atto 3. Sho Kato, responsable d’un service chez l’équipementier japonais Nissin Seiki, déclare à ce propos : "J’ai été surpris par le faible nombre de pièces utilisées par BYD et Tesla."
Le centre japonais de recherche automobile Next Generation Vehicle Center Hamamatsu a démonté la chaîne de traction électrique d’un BYD Atto 3, acheté spécialement pour cette étude. Et selon les conclusions, BYD fabrique lui-même une grande partie de ce qui est le plus coûteux dans ses véhicules, c’est-à-dire les batteries, le moteur électrique, l’électronique de puissance et les semi-conducteurs.
BYD réduit donc au maximum la dépendance envers les équipementiers et évite une partie des marges ajoutées à chaque étape. Selon le cabinet de recherche Rhodium Group, BYD fabrique environ 80 % de ses composants de rang 1 en interne. Pour Tesla, c’est 37 %.
Le constat est proche pour la banque suisse UBS qui a étudié le BYD Seal. Selon cette analyse, 75 % de la voiture est produite en interne contre 46 % pour une Tesla Model 3 fabriquée en Chine et 35 % pour une Volkswagen ID.3. BYD travaille donc avec des entreprises externes, mais au minimum.
Ses batteries conçues en interne lui donnent l'avantage
La batterie, c’est l’autre domaine où BYD brille puisqu’à l’origine, il s'agit d'une entreprise spécialisée dans cette technologie. Le constructeur chinois est aussi le deuxième producteur mondial de batteries pour véhicules électrifiés, avec 14,7 % de part de marché derrière CATL et ses 39,9 %. Quand on sait que la batterie est l’un des composants les plus chers d’une voiture électrique, une production en interne permet de mieux gérer les coûts.
BYD cherche aussi à réduire le nombre de pièces. Son Atto 3 repose sur l’e-Platform 3.0, une base technique électrique développée par le groupe. Son ensemble électrique huit en un regroupe le moteur, la transmission, le chargeur embarqué et les unités de gestion électronique dans un même module. Pour un rendement énergétique maximal de 89 %. En regroupant les boîtiers, il y a donc moins de câbles, d’assemblage et de place perdue.
Et puis n’oublions pas que BYD a sa propre flotte de navires pour inonder le monde de ses voitures. Le constructeur chinois compte aussi s’imposer en Europe, puisqu’une usine de production en Hongrie est en train de sortir de terre, avec une montée en cadence prévue en 2027.

articles.title: Xbox Series X Gets Experimental PS5 Emulator Port, Quake II Already Running
articles.text:
Sunday, September 20th 2026
	
									
	
	
	
Xbox Series X Gets Experimental PS5 Emulator Port, Quake II Already Running
A developer has apparently gotten an experimental PS5 emulator running on the Xbox Series X. Devran Cosmo Uenal, who posted about the project on YouTube on September 8, calls it a research project that ports the open-source KytyPS5 emulator to Microsoft's console through Developer Mode. Uenal shows GEX Trilogy, Hellboy: Web of Wyrd, Marvel Cosmic Invasion, and Quake II in his game library and claims they all work with controller input, with sound working in some of them. He also says AI tools were used, but it's unclear how much of the code they wrote. Compatibility is very limited, and Uenal says a lot of work is left. 
According to him, the Xbox environment doesn't support Vulkan, which KytyPS5 uses for rendering, so the graphics side has to be adapted to DirectX. That likely means progress on the PC version won't carry over automatically. We haven't seen performance benchmarks either, but the video shows Quake II running somewhere between 25 FPS and 45 FPS. The game also dips below 20 FPS in some scenes, especially when it first boots up. There is also a marked jump in input latency that can be observed, but no numbers back it up yet.The KytyPS5 emulator itself is still in its early phases, though it has moved quickly. TechPowerUp covered it taking Demon's Souls Remake from unplayable to 30 FPS in days, and it recently got the PS5 version of GTA 5 running at up to 60 FPS on a high-end PC. Emulation usually comes at a big performance cost. Running the heavier PS5 games using this emulator will be a big challenge, since the Series X and PS5 have generally similar hardware. Lighter titles might get there, though. Nonetheless, it is a very neat technical demo and shows just how fast emulation is progressing.

articles.title: iPhone owners can now submit claims in Apple’s $250 million Siri AI settlement
articles.text:
Apple is paying $250 million to settle claims that it failed to deliver an AI-upgraded Siri — and now, eligible iPhone owners can submit a claim for a payout. If you live in the US and purchased an iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max, or any iPhone 16 model between June 10th, 2024, and March 29th, 2025, you can file a claim on the settlement’s website, as reported earlier by MacRumors.
iPhone owners can now submit claims in Apple’s $250 million Siri AI settlement
The deadline to file a claim is December 21st, 2026.
You can receive an estimated $25 per eligible device, but the settlement’s website notes that this can increase to $95 depending on how many people file claims. To file a claim, you’ll need to enter your name, contact information, and iPhone serial number on the settlement’s website before the December 21st, 2026 deadline.
The class action lawsuit alleged Apple created a “clear and reasonable consumer expectation” that new AI features previewed during WWDC 2024 would launch alongside the iPhone 16. Instead, the iPhone 16 launched with a more limited set of capabilities despite being labeled as “built for Apple Intelligence.” The company later delayed the rollout of its AI-upgraded Siri, which only just arrived with iOS 27 earlier this month. Apple has denied any wrongdoing.

articles.title: Apple Watch Series 12 et Ultra 4 : cette fonction santé bien pratique manque à l’appel
articles.text:
Les nouvelles montres connectées d'Apple embarquent un processeur profondément remanié et plusieurs fonctionnalités inédites. Pourtant, une capacité santé vieille de cinq ans ne figure tout simplement plus dans la liste du matériel compatible.
La détection automatique du lavage des mains manque étonnamment à l’appel sur les nouvelles Apple Watch Series 12 et Ultra 4. Une absence d’autant plus surprenante que cette fonction est toujours intégrée à watchOS 27 et qu’Apple continue de la documenter.
Apple Watch : cette fonction née pendant la pandémie est toujours là… sauf sur les derniers modèles
Lancée en 2020 avec watchOS 7, la détection automatique du lavage des mains permet à l’Apple Watch de reconnaître les gestes associés à cette activité et de lancer un minuteur. La fonction a depuis continué son chemin dans l’écosystème d’Apple : elle est toujours présente dans watchOS 27 et dispose encore de sa propre catégorie dans l’application Santé, y compris avec iOS 27.2.
C'est en consultant la documentation officielle consacrée au système que nos confrères de 9to5Mac ont relevé un détail pour le moins surprenant. Les Apple Watch Series 11 et Ultra 3 figurent bel et bien parmi les modèles compatibles, contrairement aux Series 12 et Ultra 4. Pour l’heure, la marque à la pomme n'a pas précisé si cette absence relevait d'une incompatibilité matérielle ou s'il s'agissait d'une une simple omission dans la liste des appareils pris en charge.
Une fonction dont l’absence reste inexpliquée
Reste désormais à savoir pourquoi les deux nouvelles montres ne figurent pas dans la liste des appareils compatibles. Comme nous venons de l'évoquer, Apple n’a donné aucune explication sur ce point, et rien ne permet pour l’instant d’affirmer que les Series 12 et Ultra 4 sont techniquement incapables de gérer la détection du lavage des mains. Pour tout vous dire, cela serait d'ailleurs assez surprenant.
Une différence matérielle pourrait malgré tout expliquer cette absence, même s’il peut aussi simplement s’agir d’une omission dans la documentation. Les nouvelles générations inaugurent notamment une nouvelle puce, avec plusieurs fonctions inédites liées à l’audio et à l’intelligence artificielle. En l'état, aucun élément ne permet cependant de relier ces changements à l’absence de la fonction sur les deux nouvelles montres.
Quoi qu'il en soit, pour les propriétaires des Series 11 et Ultra 3, rien ne change pour vous : la fonctionnalité reste prise en charge. Pour les Series 12 et Ultra 4, en revanche, le mystère reste entier quant à sa prise en charge.

articles.title: Sánchez reclama “un nuevo contrato social” para abordar la IA: “La autorregulación no funciona”
articles.text:
Sánchez reclama “un nuevo contrato social” para abordar la IA: “La autorregulación no funciona”
El presidente del Gobierno presenta medidas para adaptar a España a esta nueva tecnología y anuncia que convocará a los agentes sociales para abordarlo
“Debemos impulsar un nuevo contrato social para la inteligencia artificial (IA): necesitamos un gran acuerdo de país entre sindicatos, patronal, trabajadores, partidos y poderes públicos para ofrecer seguridad a las personas ante los cambios en el trabajo y en la vida que esta tecnología va a suponer”. El presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, ha dicho eso en el marco de la presentación de IA360: plan para un despliegue de la IA, un conjunto de medidas para que España afronte de manera holística el impacto social de esta tecnología. Sánchez ha anunciado también que el Ejecutivo convocará el mes que viene a los agentes sociales de este país “para avanzar desde ya” en este gran acuerdo.
El plan, según ha explicado, constará de cuatro puntos principales, que deberán desplegarse en los próximos 12 meses. El más relevante es la intención del Gobierno de construir ese gran consenso de país sobre IA, que deberá servir para fijar la hoja de ruta de todas las actuaciones dirigidas a abordar uno de los grandes temas de nuestro tiempo.
El texto del plan recoge que se constituirán mesas sectoriales para contar con todos los actores relevantes y abordar las transiciones necesarias, desde la educación, el mercado de trabajo, el sistema financiero o el mundo de la cultura, entre otros. También se impulsará la creación de un observatorio permanente para analizar la evolución e impacto de la IA en el mercado laboral y una mesa específica con representantes del sector de la cultura para reflexionar acerca de su impacto sobre la creación y su dimensión cultural y económica, así como de su gobernanza.
Otro de los aspectos incluidos en el plan es reforzar el músculo tecnológico de España en el sector. El presidente ha destacado en este capítulo el proyecto de construcción en España de una de las siete gigafactorías de IA que quiere desarrollar la UE (grandes complejos con procesadores específicos para IA, alta conectividad y demás infraestructura necesaria para desarrollar esta tecnología). También ha resaltado los desarrollos ya en marcha junto al Barcelona Supercomputing Center (BSC) de nuevos modelos de IA para casos de uso en la lucha frente a la emergencia climática, la energía o la salud y el apoyo al desarrollo de centros de datos “que cuenten con los mejores estándares energéticos y medioambientales y respeten nuestros recursos naturales”.
El tercer punto del plan tiene que ver con hacer que la IA sea un motor económico y un semillero de talento. En este sentido, Sánchez ha dicho que el objetivo del Gobierno es que para 2030 la mitad de las pymes tengan integrada la IA generativa en sus procesos. Para que eso sea posible, asegura, hay que incidir también en la formación. “Vamos a adaptar el currículo de secundaria y de Formación Profesional para que los jóvenes aprendan a convivir de forma responsable y productiva con la IA, y para que esta tecnología no perjudique su proceso de aprendizaje”, ha dicho el presidente.
El cuarto punto de su plan tiene que ver con construir “una gobernanza de IA adecuada que nos permita afrontar estos retos”. “Los riesgos de una IA sin control son cada vez más evidentes”, ha subrayado. Sea esa amenaza real o alentada por intereses económicos de las grandes corporaciones en las que se desarrolla la IA, “el flanco de la ciberseguridad debe ser básico”. En este sentido, Sánchez ha anunciado el “refuerzo del escudo de ciberseguridad” y el aumento de la supervisión en los llamados modelos de frontera, los más avanzados del mundo.
El presidente ha hecho estas declaraciones en el mismo día en el que emprende un viaje a Nueva York para participar en la cumbre de Naciones Unidas de esta semana, en la que se hablará, entre otras cosas, de IA. También tiene previsto reunirse con el alcalde de la ciudad, Zohran Mamdani, uno de los referentes del progresismo de ese país y un destacado antagonista del presidente de EE UU, Donald Trump, partidario de una IA sin regulación.
Tecnooligarcas y autorregulación
El discurso de Sánchez ha recurrido a referencias históricas para ilustrar el momento que atraviesa ahora mismo el mundo. “A finales del siglo XIX, EE UU iniciaba la llamada edad dorada, en la que se acumularon grandes fortunas. William Henry Vanderbilt, uno de los magnates ferroviarios, dijo: ‘Al diablo con la gente, yo solo trabajo para mis accionistas”.
El presidente del Gobierno ha trazado un paralelismo entre los oligarcas de finales del siglo XIX y los de principios del XXI. “Si hay algo que la industria demuestra es que la autorregulación no funciona. Los incentivos de unos pocos que controlan las empresas punteras nunca van a estar alineados con los de la humanidad. Eso está pasando ahora con la IA”.
Por eso, asegura, hay que actuar con urgencia. “Una IA desregulada, opaca, en estampida y en manos de unos pocos es el cóctel perfecto para que ocurra una desgracia. Es evidente que el desafío de la IA ya no es para dentro de cinco, 10 o 50 años. Es para ahora mismo. Y da la sensación de que llegamos un poco tarde. Si una industria como la IA queda concentrada en unas pocas manos y países, vamos a ir mal. Por eso hay que regular”, ha insistido.
La presentación del Plan para un despliegue responsable de la IA se produce en un momento convulso en la industria, después de que algunas de las mayores desarrolladoras de IA del mundo manifestaran temores respecto a sus productos (pero, en vez de suspender su producción, han manifestado su interés en que se regule el sector).
Sánchez ha valorado el potencial transformador de la IA para la economía y la sociedad. “La IA puede reducir muchas brechas sociales, o puede ensancharlas”, tanto en el entorno laboral o educativo como en el de la ciberseguridad. El debate, ha dicho, no es si esta tecnología debe desarrollarse, sino en qué condiciones debe hacerlo. “Necesitamos una IA con supervisión y con trazabilidad para que ayude a tomar las mejores decisiones allí donde el interés público debe prevalecer”.

articles.title: Qui sème la vanne récolte le ban : des pseudos injurieux sur WoW Forever amènent Blizzard à exclure des joueurs
articles.text:
C’est l’une des nouvelles fonctionnalités de World of Warcraft: Forever, dont la bêta tourne depuis le 17 septembre : les personnages jouables portent désormais un prénom et un nom. Pour les fans de jeu de rôle, c’est l’occasion rêvée de mettre en place une expérience encore plus immersive, par exemple en partageant un même nom de famille avec d’autres.
Bien sûr, cette nouveauté donne aussi lieu à des créations très inventives : jeux de mots, clins d’œil entre initiés, blagues bien senties ou références à la pop-culture ou aux mèmes. On a par exemple vu un Barack Gnobama (bien sûr, c’était un gnome) ou un Hearthas Menethil (un paladin, clin d’œil à un certain… Arthas Menethil).
Petit rappel pour celles et ceux qui n’ont pas suivi la BlizzCon : World of Warcraft Forever a été dévoilé le 12 septembre, et Blizzard le présente comme une troisième version permanente de son MMO, à côté du WoW moderne et de WoW Classic. L’idée : repartir de l’Azeroth des origines, niveau maximum bloqué à 60, mais en l’enrichissant de nouvelles zones, de plus de 1 000 quêtes et d’une nouvelle race. En somme, le fameux « Classic+ » que la communauté réclamait depuis des années.
Tout cela ne vise pas à assouvir les envies de RP de la communauté. Comme Forever n’a pas de serveurs séparés, cette combinaison évite de bloquer des pseudonymes populaires (vous pourrez voir plein d’Arwen, par exemple) grâce à l’existence du patronyme. Ainsi, la probabilité de tomber sur une identité déjà réservée lors de la création d’un personnage est très réduite.
Globalement, l’idée est franchement appréciée. « J’adore l’effet immersif des doubles noms ❤️ », lit-on dans un fil de discussion sur le subreddit dédié à WoW Classic. « Une compilation des noms que j’ai trouvés dans le jeu et qui m’ont fait sourire », partage un internaute. Un autre propose de partager les meilleures idées des « combinaisons de prénoms et de noms de famille amusantes pour Forever ».
Mais cette personnalisation est aussi source de francs dérapages. L’outil a été largement détourné pour faire des vannes ou des jeux de mots qui ne collent plus tout à fait avec les règles établies par Blizzard. Conséquence de ces sorties de piste ? Blizzard fait sauter l’accès à la bêta des comptes qui ont enfreint ses conditions d’utilisation.
Blizzard fait le ménage dans les noms
Sur ses forums, Vrakthris, un représentant du support de Blizzard, a posé les choses : les règles de nommage valent aussi en bêta, et les enfreindre peut coûter cher. Les joueurs punis reçoivent un e-mail précisant le nom en cause, et peuvent déposer un recours — même si, de l’aveu du même modérateur, aucun des cas croisés jusqu’ici ne lui semblait mériter un pardon.
Se faire retirer l’accès n’est pas anodin pour tout le monde. On entre dans la bêta de deux façons : en s’inscrivant gratuitement et en étant tiré au sort, ou en ayant précommandé l’un des deux packs payants qui l’incluent, le pack épique ou le pack Collection. Pour ces derniers, un nom mal choisi revient donc à perdre un accès qu’ils ont payé.
« Nous savons ce que sont les noms inappropriés et nous savons que les joueurs créent régulièrement des personnages avec ce genre de noms. Nous disposons d’une option de signalement spécialement conçue pour traiter ces cas. Certains passent entre les mailles du filet ici et là, car ils ne sont pas signalés », écrit-il.
Par ailleurs, bêta ou pas, « nos règles restent en vigueur. Les noms eux-mêmes doivent continuer à respecter nos règles de nommage ». Cela n’a évidemment rien d’inédit chez Blizzard, qui applique ces règles depuis toujours. L’arrivée du nom de famille élargit simplement les possibilités de créativité et de dérapage, mais le cadre reste inchangé.
Au sein des joueurs et des joueuses, des voix appellent également à la fermeté. Si certaines tournures peuvent prêter au débat, d’autres créations sont tout simplement trop injurieuses ou grossières pour être laissées dans le jeu. Il existe certes des filtres, mais l’inventivité des internautes suffit à les contourner.
D’autres proposent non pas une sanction de bannissement, mais que tout compte pris avec un nom insultant perde le droit d’en créer un lui-même et soit renvoyé au générateur aléatoire. Certains plaident aussi pour qu’un rappel plus explicite soit fait au moment de la création du prénom et du nom de son personnage, afin d’être dissuasif.
La bêta, qui ferme le 21 octobre, n’est qu’un galop d’essai avant l’ouverture des réservations de noms, du 27 octobre au 3 novembre, avec la règle du premier arrivé premier servi. Le jeu, lui, sortira officiellement dans la nuit du 4 au 5 novembre 2026 en France. Et clairement, celles et ceux qui rêvent d’un patronyme bien senti ont tout intérêt à le garder suffisamment présentable.

articles.title: 3 fintech companies join GIZ-backed venture debt programme in Egypt - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Egyptian fintech companies AMAN Holding, Bokra and Erada Finance have joined Scale It Forward, an initiative launched by GIZ Egypt and enpact to advance the adoption of Venture Debt in Egypt.
The Scale It Forward programme brings together financial institutions and high-growth scaleups with the aim of expanding access to non-dilutive financing, building the financial sector’s capacity to design and deliver venture debt products, and creating a structured pathway for the adoption of Venture Debt within Egypt’s entrepreneurial ecosystem.
The three financial institutions signed framework agreements with enpact during a launch ceremony in Cairo, becoming the programme’s first financial institution partners and marking their commitment to exploring and piloting venture debt solutions designed to support high-growth businesses seeking alternative financing options.
Under the programme, GIZ Egypt will provide participating financial institutions with technical assistance to support the design and deployment of venture debt products within a controlled pilot environment. AMAN Holding, Bokra and Erada Finance will also gain access to a pipeline of selected scaleups.
As part of the pilot, they will also identify promising scaleups from the programme pipeline, while selected businesses will receive tailored support to prepare for Venture Debt financing. Financial institutions will provide venture debt financing starting from the equivalent of EUR5,000 (US$5,800) per business, matched by EUR5,000 in non-repayable financial support provided through the programme.
“Today’s signing event represents the official launch of the Scale It Forward programme. By bringing together three forward-looking financial institutions, AMAN, Erada Finance, and Bokra, we are taking a significant step towards establishing venture debt as a practical and scalable financing solution that enables ambitious scaleups in the Egyptian market to scale their businesses, create jobs, and grow without sacrificing equity,” said Rawan Bassam, country manager of enpact in Egypt.

articles.title: Connections and conversations: How effective curation creates impact for art exhibitions
articles.text:
Connections and conversations: How effective curation creates impact for art exhibitions
In this photo essay, we showcase artistic highlights from the ‘One | Many’ exhibition at the India Habitat Centre.
Launched in 2014, PhotoSparks is a weekly feature from YourStory, with photographs that celebrate the spirit of creativity and innovation. In the earlier 1,015 posts, we featured an art festival, cartoon gallery. world music festival, telecom expo, millets fair, climate change expo, wildlife conference, startup festival, Diwali rangoli, and jazz festival.
The India Habitat Centre (IHC) recently hosted the art exhibition titled ‘One | Many’ (see our coverage of earlier exhibitions at this popular cultural hub in New Delhi here). Curated by artist Pabitra Pal, it featured the works of 12 artists.
Such exhibitions illustrate how an effective curator connects artworks, artists, ideas, and audiences (see also Part I of our photo essay on this showcase). Tactful and strategic selection, interpretation and presentation of artworks can create a meaningful exhibition experience.
A curator connects artworks to history, culture, social issues, artistic movements, and the artist's practice. This helps audiences discover deeper interpretations of diverse art works.
Furthermore, thoughtful placement, sequencing, lighting, labels, and spatial design influence how visitors move through the exhibition and engage with the displayed works. Such placements encourage dialogue and create opportunities for reflection and learning.
Over the years, Pabitra Pal and his artistic community have organised and participated in many exhibitions. “Our latest exhibition, ‘One | Many’, became our 28th group exhibition,” Pal tells YourStory, with pride.
When he moved from Kolkata to New Delhi in 2010, he joined the artistic collective called The Mirror Group. It was established in 2002 by Dev Dutta, Susnato Chatterjee, and other artists.
The present group, some of whose artworks are showcased here, includes Dev Dutta, Debangsu Biswas, Susnato Chatterjee, Titas Das, and Soumen Basu. “We have known each other for more than 25 years, and our friendship has grown alongside our artistic practices,” Pal affirms.
“We regularly invite other artists to join us, share ideas, and celebrate the continuing journey. For us, the group is a space for friendship, discussion, exchange, and artistic growth,” he adds.
Curators thus build artistic and cultural value by bringing to the fore new artists and challenging established conventions. But all this is easier said than done.
Exhibition curators can face challenges in balancing artistic quality, diversity, theme, and the overall story without overcrowding the exhibition. Managing limited funds, gallery dimensions, transportation, insurance, installation, and deadlines are other tasks to manage.
From an audience point of view, the exhibition should be accessible to different levels of knowledge – while also preserving artistic depth and complexity. Curators need to be conscious of avoiding tokenism while addressing cultural sensitivities.
Curators therefore need to begin by defining the central question or theme, and mapping out what the exhibition wants visitors to think, feel or discover. In addition to quality and relevance of the individual artworks, relationships between the exhibits also need to enabled.
The exhibition space should support the art rather than compete or interfere with it. Varied interpretive materials will be needed, which can involve testing and experimentation with audiences from different backgrounds.
Observing visitor responses and reflecting on their feedback helps reveal insights for future exhibitions. A great exhibition is thus more than a collection of artworks – it is a carefully constructed conversation between art, artist, space, and audience.
Curator Pal’s own artistic journey began at the age of 12. “I grew up near Kolkata, West Bengal, where village and city life came together. This early experience created a strong connection between myself, nature and everyday life,” he recalls.
He later moved to Santiniketan to study at Kala Bhavana, Visva Bharati University. “Being surrounded by artists, teachers and scholars gave me the opportunity to exchange ideas, observe different artistic practices, and develop my own way of seeing,” he explains.
“My practice has developed through drawing, printmaking, painting, and three-dimensional work. I regularly experiment with different materials and techniques, but I view the medium as mainly a tool to express an idea,” Pal affirms.
His artworks connect memory, nature, everyday experience, and dreams. “Over the years, travelling and living in different places in India has also influenced my artistic thinking. My interactions and discussions with other artists have helped me continue my research and develop my practice,” he adds.
Pal has participated in more than 35 exhibitions in India and overseas, and won a string of awards. “I work as an art educator and teach visual arts through the IB curriculum. Teaching, research, observation, and making art continue to influence one another in my journey,” he explains.
“For me, making art is an ongoing process of looking, experimenting, questioning, and discovering. Each artwork develops through this process, where the material, image, memory, and idea gradually come together,” Pal says.
He also offers tips for aspiring artists “Everyone is creative — you just have to nurture it. Draw, doodle, paint, sculpt, do anything that helps you grow,” he suggests.
“Don't worry about being perfect; just keep creating, a little every day. When you travel, visit the museums of the city — they teach you about culture, heritage and the soul of a place,” he adds.
There is beauty all around. “When you see something beautiful in nature, don't just click a photo. Pause. Look with your own eyes. Make a small sketch instead. A photo is a copy, but a sketch holds your feeling, your time, your memory — something you will treasure forever,” he describes.
“Art is not about talent alone. It is about practice, patience and love for what you do," he says.
"So keep your hands busy and your heart open. The world needs your creativity,” Pal signs off.
Now what have you done today to pause in your busy schedule and harness your creative side for a better world?
(All photographs taken by Madanmohan Rao on location at IHC.)

articles.title: From an IIT Bombay Lab to a ₹1,000 Crore IPO
articles.text:
From an IIT Bombay lab to a Rs 1,000 Cr IPO
In this episode, Professor Shashikanth (IIT Bombay) shares his journey of building SEDEMAC, a deeptech startup that has crossed Rs 1,000 crore in annual revenue, Rs 1,087 crore IPO earlier this year and the stock growing over a 100% since.
India’s startup ecosystem has become very good at building companies at speed. Professor Shashikanth believes building genuinely new technology is a different game altogether.
Nearly two decades ago, a group emerging from an IIT Bombay lab started Sedemac with an ambition that sounds deceptively simple: build new control technologies and see them achieve widespread adoption.
Today, the numbers tell a remarkable story. Sedemac has crossed Rs 1,000 crore in annual revenue, with around Rs 200 crore in EBITDA, Rs 150 crore in profit before tax and Rs 100 crore in profit after tax. The company operates at roughly 40% return on capital employed, ships one million motor controllers every quarter, and its technology sits inside millions of two-wheelers on Indian roads.
But Shashikanth’s story is less about one company’s growth and more about what happens when engineers attempt something that the market itself may not yet know it needs.
“Creators of technology are market creators,” he says. “You don’t start with, ‘Oh, this market is going to grow big.’ Therefore, it will grow big or not because of you.”
Solving a problem the market was not asking to solve
At the heart of Sedemac’s growth is its work on motor controllers and sensorless commutation. A motor controller manages the flow of power between a power source such as a battery and an electric machine. For that motor to operate, the controller needs to determine which coils should be energised based on the position of the rotor. Conventionally, a physical sensor can provide that information.
Sensorless commutation attempts to do this without such a physical position sensor, instead estimating the rotor’s position using other information.
At higher speeds, this has been understood for decades. At zero and low speeds, the physics becomes significantly harder because one of the phenomena used for estimation, back EMF, reduces with speed and disappears at zero speed.
“We are the first company globally, globally, it is a very big statement, that has made as much progress in sensorless commutation as we have,” says Shashikanth.
But Sedemac did not start in 2007 with a grand plan to solve this particular problem. The opportunity emerged years later through its work with the two-wheeler industry. Around 2014-15, while developing an Integrated Starter Generator or ISG, the team realised the system could be improved if it made progress on sensorless commutation.
In 2018, a TVS moped became the first vehicle to use the system. According to Shashikanth, it was also the world’s first sensorless ISG application.
From one moped to millions of vehicles
What followed was not an overnight deep-tech success story.
Sedemac estimates that 12 to 13 million vehicles carrying its ISG are now on Indian roads. Five of the top 10 two-wheeler models selling in India use its ISG in at least one variant, including models from TVS, Bajaj and Hero.
Another Sedemac technology, Shashikanth says, has already gone into around 50 million vehicles.
This scale matters because Sedemac had to break into an industry dominated by enormous incumbent suppliers. Four manufacturers, Honda, Hero, TVS and Bajaj, account for around 85% of India’s two-wheeler market, according to numbers Shashikanth cites in the conversation. Sedemac today supplies three of those top four.
“You cannot enter and grow very rapidly unless you have something special,” he says.
The company’s approach to finding customers has remained surprisingly straightforward. Build something new, create a working demonstration, and write directly to the leaders of that industry.
“If something is really fresh, usually you will get some response.”
Getting a response, however, is only the beginning. A demonstration has to work on the customer’s equipment. Pricing has to make sense. The technology has to survive its first commercial introduction. Users have to value it. Quality problems cannot emerge. Only then can serious scaling begin.
In two-wheelers, Shashikanth says the journey from demonstration to the first introduction could take three to four years if everything went right.
And sometimes, he says, the timeline can simply be “infinity”.
Deep tech needs technical talent and adopters, not just capital
For Shashikanth, Sedemac’s journey depended on two ingredients above everything else.
The first was “extraordinary technical ability”.
The second was having large, sophisticated customers capable of adopting what those engineers created.
“If you have the technical smarts who are like absolute top notch in very good density and you have adopters who can potentially adopt these cool things that these people are building, then those are very good setups for that to progress.”
Capital mattered, but he places it below those two factors.
In 2008, Nexus invested ₹2 crore in Sedemac. Shashikanth acknowledges that without an ecosystem willing to finance engineers without substantial capital of their own, the company might never have emerged.
But he draws a sharp distinction between enabling a business and creating one.
“Investors are betting on that business doing well,” he says. “They can never create the business. They can only support it.”
That distinction also shapes his view of India’s deep-tech ecosystem. Funding can create infrastructure, support experimentation and give engineers the runway to try difficult things. But money alone cannot manufacture technical excellence.
“You can never produce the talent just by throwing some money.”
The best engineers come for the work, not the vision statement
Sedemac today has roughly 250 engineers, with Shashikanth estimating that 60 to 70% come from IITs, NITs and BITS.
His philosophy for attracting them is unusually unsentimental.
“I feel that most employees, if you ask them honestly, they don’t care a damn about your vision.”
Instead, he argues that exceptional technical people primarily care about the quality of the work and whether they are rewarded fairly.
“The absolute top thing is that you should have high quality work. Otherwise the high quality employee will not come.”
Culture comes after those fundamentals. At Sedemac, he describes a workplace where hierarchy carries less weight than the strength of an argument. “If you’re talking nonsense, people will say you’re talking nonsense.”
For a technology company, this engineering density is not merely a hiring advantage. It is the engine that allows the company to repeatedly create new technologies.
As Shashikanth puts it, Sedemac’s achievement is not only sensorless commutation. More importantly, “we built an engine that can build such technologies”.
₹36 crore to ₹1,058 crore, but profitability is the bigger statement
Sedemac’s revenue was around ₹8 crore in 2014, ₹18 crore in 2015 and ₹36 crore in 2016. By FY26, Shashikanth said it had reached ₹1,058 crore, close to 30 times its 2016 revenue.
ISG became the biggest growth contributor from FY19 onwards, while the company is also pursuing opportunities across generators, electric vehicles and power tools.
Yet Shashikanth is particularly emphatic about another set of numbers: profitability and capital efficiency.
His argument is provocative. If a company claims to have created genuinely differentiated technology, that differentiation should eventually translate into competitive advantage and pricing power.
“If you claim that you are a technology company that has succeeded, how can you not make money?”
He qualifies this as an argument about companies that have already reached scale, rather than businesses still investing to establish themselves. But once meaningful adoption has happened, he believes technological advantage should become visible in economics.
“If you do not have strong enough EBITDAs and good ROCE, you are not a technology company. Straight.”
Sedemac’s ROCE is currently around 40%, according to the conversation. For Shashikanth, there is no financial trick behind it.
“You cannot financially engineer your way into this.”
Build something fresh. Make it valuable enough that customers want it. Earn some pricing power. Keep costs and capital expenditure under control. Profitability and capital efficiency follow.
India’s deep-tech opportunity is ultimately an imagination problem
Perhaps Shashikanth’s strongest argument is that India’s constraint is not simply capital or talent. It is whether enough engineers believe they can create something the world has not already created.
He compares technological ecosystems to sport. India can produce Virat Kohli because generations of young cricketers can realistically imagine becoming world-class. Spain can produce Lionel Messi because a similar pyramid exists around football.
For engineering, he believes India still lacks that depth.
“You cannot have excellence in an ecosystem without the top of the world being in that ecosystem.”
He does see progress. More engineers can now access capital, more young people are attempting difficult problems, and India has pockets of serious technical excellence. But ecosystems take generations to build.
Sedemac itself offers one glimpse of what that future could look like: a company that began with engineers trying to build “fresh technologies”, spent years persuading large manufacturers to adopt them, and eventually saw those technologies disappear almost invisibly into everyday products used by millions of Indians.
The lesson is not that every deep-tech company needs to follow Sedemac’s path.
It is that original technology often begins before there is an obvious market to measure, a customer asking for the solution, or even certainty that adoption will happen.

articles.title: Gmail affiche un raccourci pour vos codes d’authentification sur iOS et Android
articles.text:
Google vient de mettre à jour discrètement son client de messagerie Gmail sur iOS et Android. La firme de Mountain View a profité de l’occasion pour inaugurer une nouvelle fonctionnalité très pratique qui devrait vous faire gagner un peu de temps au quotidien.
Un raccourci pour copier vos codes d’authentification
Sur certains services en ligne, la connexion à un votre compte ne peut se faire qu’après avoir saisi un code d’authentification envoyé par email. Cela implique toutefois d’ouvrir le client de messagerie, puis l’e-mail en question, avant de pouvoir enfin copier le code en question dans le presse-papier de l’appareil pour le coller ensuite dans la fenêtre d’authentification correspondante.
Sur iOS, les utilisateurs d’iPhone qui se servent quotidiennement du client Mail n’ont pas besoin de réaliser cette gymnastique, car l’OS d’Apple affiche automatiquement les codes d’authentification reçus au-dessus du clavier sur les fenêtres de connexion. Mais ce n’était jusqu’à présent pas le cas pour Gmail.
Google a corrigé ce manquement dans la dernière mise à jour de son application, aussi bien sur iOS que sur Android. Désormais, lorsqu’une plate-forme en ligne vous envoie un code d’authentification, vous n’avez plus besoin d’ouvrir le message associé pour pouvoir copier le code en question. Gmail affiche, dès la boîte de réception, un petit raccourci permettant de copier à la volée le code contenu dans le message, dans le presse-papier de votre smartphone.
Une simple tape sur ce nouveau bouton vous permet donc de récupérer le code. Cette nouveauté a, a priori, été déployée dans la version 2026.09.07.x de Gmail sur Android, et dans la version 6.0.260907 de l’application sur iOS. Il semblerait néanmoins que Google n’active cette nouveauté que de manière progressive. Aucun de nos appareils, Android comme iOS, ne bénéficie pour l’heure de cette nouveauté à l’heure où ces lignes sont écrites.

articles.title: Avião autônomo da Joby cruza os EUA sem piloto assumir controles e pode ir muito além dos táxis aéreos elétricos
articles.text:
Um avião equipado com a tecnologia de autonomia da Joby Aviation percorreu mais de 3.100 milhas (cerca de 5 mil km) pelos Estados Unidos sem que um piloto precisasse assumir os controles. O teste usou um Cessna Caravan adaptado e teve supervisão remota na Califórnia e na Carolina do Sul.
A demonstração mostra que a tecnologia da empresa pode ir além dos táxis aéreos elétricos. Segundo a Joby, o sistema também pode ser usado em transporte médico, resposta a desastres, logística de defesa e transporte comercial de cargas.
Cruzando os EUA sem intervenção
A viagem foi feita com um Cessna Caravan modificado para receber o sistema de autonomia da Joby. A aeronave realizou de forma autônoma todas as etapas do trajeto, incluindo taxiamento, decolagem, navegação e pouso.
Um piloto permaneceu a bordo para cumprir exigências de conformidade, mas não precisou assumir o controle em nenhum momento. A operação foi supervisionada remotamente pela equipe da Joby na Califórnia e pela Shaw Air Force Base, na Carolina do Sul.
A empresa classificou a jornada como o “primeiro voo autônomo de costa a costa pelos Estados Unidos”. O avião ainda fará o caminho de volta à Costa Oeste nas próximas duas semanas, com paradas em cidades como Louisville, no Kentucky, e Salt Lake City.
Da medicina ao transporte de cargas
A tecnologia foi desenvolvida para ser instalada em diferentes aeronaves convencionais. A Joby pretende colocar primeiro no mercado uma aeronave regional equipada com o sistema, com possíveis aplicações em missões de defesa e no transporte comercial de cargas.
O voo também serviu para mostrar que a autonomia pode lidar com diferentes ambientes e missões. Entre as possibilidades citadas pela empresa estão:
- Transporte médico;
- Resposta a desastres;
- Logística de defesa;
- Transporte comercial de cargas;
- Operação autônoma de aeronaves convencionais.
A Joby é conhecida principalmente pelo desenvolvimento de aeronaves elétricas de decolagem e pouso vertical, os eVTOLs, destinadas a transportar passageiros em trajetos curtos nas cidades.
A companhia também mantém uma relação de longa data com o Departamento de Defesa dos EUA e vem ampliando sua atuação nesse setor.
O desenvolvimento do sistema autônomo conta com um contrato de US$ 17 milhões (cerca de R$ 87 milhões) da Força Aérea dos EUA por meio da AFWERX. A Joby planeja usar a tecnologia em uma aeronave regional que também poderá atender ao transporte comercial de cargas.
Aquisição reforça os projetos militares
Em agosto, a Joby adquiriu a Resonant Sciences por US$ 500 milhões (cerca de R$ 2,56 bilhões), em dinheiro e ações. A empresa, sediada em Ohio, desenvolve sistemas de radiofrequência e sensores e passou a integrar uma divisão de defesa da Joby.
Leia mais:
- Carros voadores já têm “aeroporto” sendo testado em SP
- Eve: carro voador da Embraer terá produção em série em Taubaté
- Em breve, os céus podem ser tomados por carros voadores e aviões supersônicos
Essa divisão reúne projetos de aeronaves híbridas elétricas movidas a turbinas, modelos elétricos a hidrogênio e sistemas de autonomia.
No ano passado, a Joby assinou um acordo com a L3Harris Technologies para “explorar oportunidades” de desenvolvimento de uma nova classe de aeronaves para aplicações de defesa. A proposta envolve um modelo híbrido de decolagem e pouso vertical, movido por turbina a gás e capaz de voar de forma autônoma.
O voo pelos Estados Unidos coloca a tecnologia de autonomia da Joby em uma operação de escala maior, enquanto a empresa continua desenvolvendo seus táxis aéreos elétricos.
Valdir Antonelli é jornalista com especialização em marketing digital e consumo.

articles.title: En silencio, Disney+ apuntala una tendencia ya generalizada en las plataformas de streaming: anuncios para todos
articles.text:
Cuando llegó Netflix, parecía que la televisión convencional tenía los días contados. Contar con un amplio catálogo y sin anuncios era algo revolucionario. y luego se fueron sumando más plataformas como HBO y Disney+. La plataforma de Disney apareció en 2020 con catálogo interesante y la posibilidad de tenerlo todo por 69,99 euros al año o 6,99 euros al mes. Seis años más tarde ya son 159,90 euros al año en el plan premium y acaban de actualizar sus políticas para avisar de un cambio importante.
Ni pagando la tarifa máxima te vas a librar de anuncios.
En corto. Se hacían eco nuestros compañeros de Espinof: Disney+ ha modificado sus condiciones de uso para poder obligar a todos sus usuarios, sin importar el plan, a ver publicidad. Hay un plan específico con publi que seguirá como hasta ahora, pero el cambio es que los dos sin esta molestia (Estándar y Premium) también "pueden incluir contenido promocional". El punto el el siguiente:
Disney+ también ofrece planes para ver películas y series sin interrupciones publicitarias: Disney+ Estándar y Disney+ Prémium. No obstante, pueden incluir contenido promocional limitado, anuncios o promociones antes o después de la reproducción de contenidos, clips y tráileres de contenidos, productos y servicios de Disney, además de contenido patrocinado o de otras marcas. El contenido en directo o los eventos especiales (reposiciones incluidas) pueden incluir pausas publicitarias o mensajes publicitarios.
Dejan claro que essa publicidad es tanto de contenidos de la plataforma, del grupo o de marcas que quieran pagar, por lo que puede ocurrir como en Amazon, esta tranquilamente viendo una batalla de 'Los Anillos de Poder' y te interrumpa uno que te ofrece saber cuánto vale tu coche. Para reforzar este cambio, hay otro punto en el que se evidencia que no se refieren sólo al plan con anuncios:
Si te suscribes a Disney+ Estándar con anuncios, verás anuncios durante las películas y las series. También es posible que veas algunos anuncios antes o durante la reproducción de contenido en nuestros otros planes"
Bloqueadores de publi. Los únicos que se salvan son los perfiles junior, ya que esos no tienen publicidad, pero aparte de las nuevas condiciones, Disney+ también ha pensado en quienes puedan usar programas que bloqueen la publicidad. Como aquí no es un descuido, sino algo deliberado por parte del usuario, la compañía se reserva tres tipos de acciones:
- Suspender o cancelar tanto la suscripción como la posibilidad de acceder a la cuenta.
- Ofrecer al suscriptor un plan más adecuado para el uso que le da.
- Bloquear la visualización del contenido hasta que aceptes las nuevas condiciones.
Mierdificación. Decíamos que la llegada de Netflix y Disney+ parecía un puñal para la televisión convencional y, curiosamente, lo mismo se dijo de los grandes streamers en Twitch. Al final, las plataformas han terminado siendo como la televisión convencional (incluso con sus programas y elencos) y los grandes streamers, directamente, han copiado el formato de esa televisión. El movimiento de Disney+ es uno que ya no sorprende porque nos hemos acostumbrado tanto estos últimos meses a que vayan embarrando cada vez más las experiencias que es, simplemente, una más.
Una vez que una empresa tiene una base de usuarios que considera correcta, empieza a empeorar las condiciones y la experiencia. Anuncios, retirada de contenidos, disminución de opciones o restricciones evidentes a la vez que suben el precio es algo que hacen independientemente de si son apps de vídeo por streaming, de música, de videojuegos como PlayStation Plus o GamePass (suben precio, luego lo bajan quitando juegos y siendo más alto que antes de la subida anterior) y hasta los chatbots. En inglés, eso se conoce como 'enshittification' o mierdificación, y básicamente es hacer de forma deliberada que el producto sea peor cada cierto tiempo.
Y el problema es que estamos en un momento en el que parece que ninguna quiere destacar, precisamente, por desmarcarse de esa mierdificación.

articles.title: 👨🏿🚀TechCabal Daily – Kenya eyes Dangote IPO | TechCabal
articles.text:
Happy salary week. 💸️
A few readers wrote back to say they couldn’t access the Citi Foundation funding link. We’ve fixed that. The foundation is offering up to $500,000 to organisations building solutions that prepare young people for AI. Apply by October 6.
Reminder: We’re looking for stories from people whose journeys changed at Moonshot. Met a co-founder, investor, partner, or future employer there? Tell us about it.
Let’s get into today’s dispatch.
Read smart insights about Francophone Africa’s tech ecosystem—weekly.
Capital Markets
Kenya wants a slice of Dangote’s landmark oil listing
Africa’s largest initial public offering (IPO) is officially underway in Lagos, Nigeria. Dangote Petroleum Refinery opened a ₦2.15 trillion ($1.6 billion) share sale on September 14, valuing the massive facility at ₦63 trillion ($47.6 billion).
Catch-up: In May, Aliko Dangote, Africa’s richest man, teased a secondary listing on the London Stock Exchange, but management recently paused international debuts for three years to build a solid track record. Seeing an opening, Frank Mwiti, chief executive officer of Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE), is pushing to bring East African investors into the offer before pursuing a future cross-listing in Kenya.
Between the lines: Formal stock exchange cross-listings usually drag on through years of regulatory red tape, yet retail fintech apps are leaping over traditional hurdles. Platforms like Bamboo already enable IPO subscriptions in countries such as Uganda, Tanzania, and Rwanda, while Kenyan fintech Cloud9 allows local retail users to participate directly from their mobile phones.
Mwiti’s strategy smartly leverages this immediate retail enthusiasm first, using bottom-up consumer appetite to create market momentum before tackling the complex regulatory machinery needed for a full cross-listing in Nairobi.
Why it matters: Cross-border equity sales inside the continent remain rare because of strict currency controls and fragmented clearing systems. Retail fintechs and progressive exchange leaders are constructing a linked African capital market without waiting for formal multilateral treaties.
What to watch: Mwiti is using these Lagos talks to construct a broader energy pipeline on the Nairobi floor. Local Dangote supply ventures, renewable energy firms, and fuel logistics operators could follow. Infrastructure projects like the East African Crude Oil Pipeline might eventually tap regional equity markets instead of relying purely on expensive foreign loans.
Every business owner needs to watch this.
The business questions you Google, answered by experts. Watch for free .
Telecoms
Safaricom is the latest to weigh in on the Safaricom stake-sale saga
After Kenya’s High Court blocked the government’s sale of a 15% stake in Safaricom to Vodacom on September 15, every party with a vested interest in that deal is now appealing the decision. The latest is Safaricom itself, Kenya’s largest telecom company, the acquiree, which says it is reviewing the judgment and its implications.
What happened? In July, Kenya finalised the sale of its 15% stake in Safaricom to Vodacom for KES 204.3 billion ($1.6 billion). The deal pushed Vodacom’s stake in the telecom company to 55%, giving it majority control. But in September, the High Court declared the sale unlawful and ordered the shares returned to the state.
The ruling has triggered a new round of legal wrangling. Kenya’s government and Vodacom have both said they will appeal, with Vodacom also seeking to pause the court’s order while the appeal is heard. Now Safaricom says it is reviewing the judgment and will provide updates as the legal process continues.
Explain like I’m new here: This is the same deal that has been moving between Kenyan courts for months. In June, the Kenyan Court of Appeal lifted an earlier order blocking the transaction, allowing it to close in July. The High Court has now gone the other way, saying the sale did not meet constitutional and legal requirements around public participation and transparency.
Why does this matter? This is bigger than who owns 15% of Safaricom. The sale gave the Kenyan government KES 204.3 billion ($1.6 million) in cash, while another KES 40.2 billion ($311,000) was paid upfront for rights linked to future dividends from its remaining 20% stake. The government had planned to use the proceeds to fund development projects without adding to public debt.
If the ruling survives the appeal, Kenya could have to unwind the share sale while figuring out what happens to the money it has already received. Vodacom could also lose the 15% stake that gave it majority control.
Zoom out: Safaricom is one of Kenya’s most valuable corporate assets, and M-PESA, its mobile money arm, makes it central to the country’s financial and digital economy. That makes the ownership fight unusually consequential. For now, the company has a majority owner on paper, a court order challenging that ownership, and several appeals still to play out.
Don’t miss Moonshot 2026 for anything in the world!
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. We’ve filtered the noise out of Moonshot 2026, optimising the conference strictly for high-calibre connections between startup founders, global financial operators, enterprise leaders and individuals rewiring Africa’s technical frameworks. Join us on October 28 & 29, 2026. Get your ticket .
Banking
Investec’s UK expansion is starting to get expensive
Investec’s UK business is starting to look like the awkward part of an otherwise healthy growth story. South Africa’s fifth-largest commercial bank expects its upcoming half-year results to show higher earnings overall, but its UK business is heading in the opposite direction.
What happened? On Friday, Investec said adjusted operating profit at its UK Specialist Bank is expected to fall by 3% to 7% from the previous period. Across the group, however, adjusted earnings per share (EPS) are still expected to reach 7%. South Africa is doing much of the heavy lifting, with operating profit expected to rise 6% in rand terms.
Explain like I’m new here: Investec is a bit unusual. It started in South Africa but now has major operations in both South Africa and the UK. The UK business includes corporate banking, wealth management, and specialist lending. It is also where Investec has been investing heavily to become a bigger, more mainstream bank.
That investment is starting to show up in the numbers. The UK business has been hiring relationship managers and building out its corporate banking team. In July, Investec said it was building a dedicated mid-market team expected to grow to more than 40 relationship managers. The lender appointed Terry Koizou to lead client relationship management at its UK corporate banking arm.
Why now? Investec is not pulling back from the UK. It is doing the opposite. The bank is trying to turn its UK operation into a larger growth engine while also expanding its reach across Europe.
That helps explain its push for an Irish banking licence. Investec already operates in Ireland, but a fuller banking setup would give it more room to serve corporate and wealthy clients across the European Union (EU). Its existing Irish branch is currently an Investec Bank plc branch regulated by the Central Bank of Ireland for conduct of business.
Between the lines: There’s a bet hiding underneath these numbers. Investec is accepting some near-term pressure in the UK as it spends to build a bigger franchise. The question is whether that investment eventually produces enough new clients, lending, and wealth-management income to justify the extra cost.
And South Africa gives it some breathing room. Investec said revenue growth has been supported by higher lending activity and strong inflows into its South African wealth business, where funds under management rose 13.8% since March.
Zoom out: Investec is trying to become less of a South African bank with an international arm and more of a genuinely international specialist bank. The UK is central to that ambition, and Ireland could become another piece of the European puzzle. For now, though, the numbers show expansion is not free.
Telecoms
Safaricom hits a million subscribers as Kenya’s fibre divide widens
Laying cables underground is an expensive business venture. Mobile coverage dominates everyday headlines, yet fixed home broadband offers a major competitive advantage.
Fresh data from the Communications Authority of Kenya (CAK), the country’s telecom regulator, show Safaricom has become the first provider to cross one million fixed subscriptions. At 1,024,950 users, it claims 36.1% of the market. Jamii Telecommunications trails at 19.1%, while former pioneer Wananchi Group retains 10.4%.
Between the lines: The massive gulf highlights how unforgiving physical infrastructure can be. Running last-mile fibre demands relentless capital investment that few balance sheets can sustain over time.
Airtel Africa recently decided to wind up its Kenyan wholesale fibre entity after accumulating losses of KES 16.1 million ($125,000) and generating zero commercial revenue over two years. Airtel targeted enterprise wholesale clients rather than residential households, yet its departure underscores the same economic reality. Running wired networks in Kenya without massive scale leads straight to a dead end.
Why it matters: Locking in one million households gives Safaricom an unbeatable digital runway inside local living rooms. Once fixed Internet is installed, it becomes the essential anchor for smart home devices, streaming services, and digital tools. Competitors find it nearly impossible to convince users to switch.
What to watch: Challengers are turning to wireless technologies to survive. Poa Internet holds 8.8% market share through cheap fixed wireless, while satellite newcomer Starlink holds 1.0%. Even so, in lucrative urban centres, Safaricom has constructed a lead that looks nearly impossible to crack.

articles.title: Joindre son enfant, le localiser, être alerté : ce forfait mobile pense à tout, sans smartphone — Frandroid
articles.text:
Le premier téléphone est souvent un casse-tête pour les parents, partagés entre l’envie de joindre leur enfant et la crainte de l’exposer trop tôt à internet. L’opérateur SFR propose une solution intermédiaire avec son Pack Kids Protégés, disponible depuis le 18 août 2026. Il associe la montre connectée Honor Choice Kids Watch Plus à un forfait mobile 5 Go dédié, sur le réseau de SFR, évidemment.
Le pack revient à 14,99 euros par mois, ou 7,99 euros par mois pour les clients d’une box SFR, plus 1 euro à la commande. Une offre repérée par notre comparateur de forfaits mobiles.
Ce pack en bref :
- Montre connectée Honor Choice Kids Watch Plus avec carte SIM intégrée
- Appels limités aux contacts autorisés, géolocalisation en temps réel et bouton SOS
- Forfait 5 Go dédié et bloqué sur le réseau de SFR, sans engagement
- Ni internet, ni réseaux sociaux, ni téléchargement d’applications
- Montre à 1 euro à la commande puis 3 euros par mois pendant 24 mois
En ce moment, le Pack Kids Protégés de SFR est disponible à partir de 14,99 euros par mois sur le réseau de SFR, directement sur le site de SFR.
Pour la rentrée, BNP Paribas propose une offre de bienvenue étudiante avec carte Visa incluse, paiements sans frais à l’étranger, prêt à 0,99% et jusqu’à 175€ d’avantages offerts (80€ offerts + 1 an gratuit à Esprit Libre).
40 Go
- Appels illimités
- 40 Go en France
- 40 Go en Europe
2h/1 Go
- 2h d’appels
- 1 Go en France
- 1 Go en Europe
200 Go
- Appels illimités
- 200 Go en France
- 100 Go en Europe
Une montre pensée pour la sécurité, pas pour la distraction
La Honor Choice Kids Watch Plus n’est pas une montre connectée grand public. Grâce à sa carte SIM intégrée, elle passe des appels et se géolocalise seule, sans qu’un téléphone soit nécessaire à proximité de l’enfant. Les appels sont limités à un cadre de contacts autorisés, définis par les parents, et un bouton SOS permet de lancer une alerte en cas de besoin. La géolocalisation en temps réel, via l’application parentale, aide à suivre les trajets quotidiens et les activités.
Aussi, la montre ne donne accès ni à internet, ni aux réseaux sociaux, ni au téléchargement d’applications. Elle embarque aussi un mode Classe pour rester discrète pendant les cours, et une certification IP68 qui la protège des éclaboussures. L’idée, c’est de pouvoir joindre son enfant et le laisser sortir seul, sans lui donner un smartphone complet trop tôt.
Un forfait bloqué et sans engagement, mais une montre à régler sur deux ans
Le forfait associé est un 5 Go dédié, spécialement conçu pour fonctionner avec la montre. Il est bloqué, c’est-à-dire qu’il ne donne accès à aucune data libre ni navigation internet, ce qui garantit le cadre sécurisé et évite tout dépassement. Il conserve en revanche un vrai numéro de téléphone, pour que l’enfant reste joignable. Ce forfait est facturé 11,99 euros par mois, ou 4,99 euros par mois pour les clients d’une box SFR grâce à une remise de 7 euros, et il est sans engagement.
À noter, le forfait est compatible 5G alors que la montre se connecte en 4G, ce qui ne change rien à l’usage puisque appels, messages et géolocalisation n’ont pas besoin de la 5G.
C’est sur la montre que se situe le vrai engagement financier. Elle est proposée à 1 euro à la commande, puis 3 euros par mois pendant 24 mois, ou 73 euros comptant. En additionnant la montre et le forfait, le pack revient donc à 14,99 euros par mois sans box, ou 7,99 euros par mois pour les clients box SFR, pendant deux ans. Le forfait reste résiliable à tout moment, mais en cas d’arrêt anticipé, les mensualités restantes de la montre demeurent dues, sauf à l’avoir réglée comptant.
